name: Nuwakot Durbar (Saat Tale Durbar)
built_century_text: 18th century; the present palace was built after Prithvi Narayan Shah conquered Nuwakot in 1801 BS (1744-45). Wikidata gives inception c. 1750.
architecture: Seven-storey brick fort-palace with 6-foot-thick walls on an 84 x 36 ft plinth, carved Newar windows (aankhi jhyal) and a glazed-tile roof, built by craftsmen from Lalitpur in Kathmandu style. Annexes include Ranga Mahal and the Garad Ghar.
short: Seven-storey hilltop palace that Prithvi Narayan Shah used as his base for the unification of Nepal.
story: You are standing on the ridge of Nuwakot, looking up at the Saat Tale Durbar, the seven-storey palace. After Prithvi Narayan Shah captured Nuwakot in 1744, he moved his capital here from Gorkha, because this ridge sits on the old trade route between the Kathmandu Valley and Tibet. Each floor had a job. Courtiers and guards waited on the ground floor, the king held meetings on the first, the royal couple slept on the second, soldiers kept watch higher up, and the fifth and sixth floors served as a prison for captured kings. Notice how thick the walls are, about six feet, more fort than home. Craftsmen from Lalitpur carved the windows you see. Look south-east to the Ranga Mahal, the old theatre hall, and east to the guard house. The 2015 earthquake badly damaged the complex, and restoration has been under way since.
facts: Prithvi Narayan Shah moved his capital from Gorkha to Nuwakot after conquering it in 1801 BS (1744-45).
The main palace has seven storeys, which is why locals call it Saat Tale (seven-storey) Durbar.
Its plinth measures 84 by 36 feet and its walls are about 6 feet thick.
The fifth and sixth floors were used as a prison; the King of Tanahun was held here.
The palace has been on Nepal's UNESCO Tentative List since 2008.

earthquake_2015: The April 2015 earthquake devastated the palace complex; it has been under restoration since, with work slowed by the pandemic.

festivals.note_np: नजिकैको भैरवी मन्दिरबाट दरबार छेउको तलेजु मन्दिरसम्म सिन्दूर दलेर निकालिने जात्रा।

quiz.q: Why is Nuwakot Durbar called 'Saat Tale'?
options: It took seven years to build
quiz.explanation: Saat Tale means seven-storey; the main palace has seven floors.
quiz.q_np: नुवाकोट दरबारलाई 'सात तले' किन भनिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: सात तले भनेको सात तल्ला हो; मुख्य दरबारमा सात तल्ला छन्।

quiz.q: Which king moved his capital from Gorkha to Nuwakot after 1744?
quiz.explanation: Prithvi Narayan Shah conquered Nuwakot in 1801 BS and based his unification campaign here.
quiz.q_np: 1744 पछि कुन राजाले आफ्नो राजधानी गोरखाबाट नुवाकोट सारे?
quiz.explanation_np: पृथ्वीनारायण शाहले 1801 वि.सं. मा नुवाकोट जितेर यहीँबाट एकीकरण अभियान सञ्चालन गरे।

quiz.q: Which floors of the palace were used as a prison?
quiz.explanation: The fifth and sixth floors held prisoners, including the King of Tanahun.
quiz.q_np: दरबारका कुन तल्लाहरू कारागारका रूपमा प्रयोग गरिन्थे?
quiz.explanation_np: पाँचौँ र छैटौँ तल्लामा तनहुँका राजासहित कैदीहरू राखिएका थिए।

quiz.q: Where did the craftsmen who built the palace come from?
quiz.explanation: Craftsmen from Lalitpur built the palace in the Kathmandu style.
quiz.q_np: दरबार बनाउने सिपालुहरू कहाँबाट आएका थिए?
quiz.explanation_np: ललितपुरका सिपालुहरूले दरबार काठमाडौँ शैलीमा बनाए।

quiz.q: How thick are the walls of the main palace?
quiz.explanation: The palace was built like a fort with walls about 6 feet thick.
quiz.q_np: मुख्य दरबारका भित्ता कति बाक्लो छन्?
quiz.explanation_np: दरबार किल्ला जस्तै बनेको छ, र भित्ताहरू करिब 6 फिट बाक्लो छन्।

clues: A conqueror left his hill capital to rule from this ridge, counting seven floors above the guards' room.
Kings once sat as prisoners on the fifth and sixth floors of this brick tower above the Trishuli valley.

model.notes: Tall narrow seven-storey brick tower with rows of dark carved windows and a small tiled lookout room on top; small pagoda temple at its side.

short_np: सात तले डाँडाको दरबार, जसलाई पृथ्वीनारायण शाहले नेपाल एकीकरणको आधारका रूपमा प्रयोग गरे।
story_np: तपाईं नुवाकोटको डाँडामा उभिएर सात तले दरबार, सात तले दरबारतिर हेर्दै हुनुहुन्छ। पृथ्वीनारायण शाहले सन् १७४४ मा नुवाकोट कब्जा गरेपछि उनले गोरखाबाट राजधानी यहीँ सारे, किनभने यो डाँडा काठमाडौँ उपत्यका र तिब्बतबीचको पुरानो व्यापारिक बाटोमा पर्छ। हरेक तलाको आफ्नै काम थियो। दरबारिया र पहरेदारहरू भुइँतलामा बस्थे, राजाले पहिलो तलामा बैठक गर्थे, शाही जोडी दोस्रो तलामा सुत्थे, सिपाहीहरू माथि पहरा दिन्थे, र पाँचौँ र छैटौँ तला कब्जामा परेका राजाहरूका लागि कारागार थिए। भित्ताहरू कति बाक्ला छन् हेर्नुहोस्, करिब छ फिट, घरभन्दा बढी किल्ला। ललितपुरका शिल्पीहरूले तपाईंले देख्ने झ्यालहरू कुँदेका थिए। दक्षिण-पूर्वमा रङ्गमहल, पुरानो नाट्यशाला, र पूर्वमा पहरा घरतिर हेर्नुहोस्। सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पले परिसरलाई ठूलो क्षति पुर्‍यायो, र पुनर्स्थापना त्यसयता चलिरहेको छ।
facts_np: पृथ्वीनारायण शाहले वि.सं. १८०१ (१७४४-४५) मा नुवाकोट जितेपछि राजधानी गोरखाबाट यहाँ सारे।
मुख्य दरबारमा सात तला छन्, त्यसैले स्थानीयले यसलाई सात तले दरबार भन्छन्।
यसको जगको नाप ८४ गुणा ३६ फिट र भित्ताहरू करिब ६ फिट बाक्लो छन्।
पाँचौँ र छैटौँ तला कारागारका रूपमा प्रयोग गरिन्थे; तनहुँका राजालाई यहीँ राखिएको थियो।
दरबार सन् २००८ देखि नेपालको युनेस्को अस्थायी सूचीमा छ।
quake_np: सन् २०१५ अप्रिलको भूकम्पले दरबार परिसरलाई ध्वस्त पार्‍यो; त्यसयता पुनर्स्थापना हुँदै आएको छ, महामारीका कारण काम ढिलो भएको छ।
clues_np: एक विजेताले आफ्नो पहाडी राजधानी छाडेर यही डाँडाबाट शासन गरे; पहरेदारको कोठामाथि सात तल्ला गनिन्छन्।
त्रिशूली उपत्यकामाथिको यो इँटाको मीनारको पाँचौँ र छैटौँ तल्लामा राजाहरू कैदी भएर बसेका थिए।

name: Bhairabi Temple, Nuwakot
built_century_text: 18th century; sources differ, some credit Jagat Jaya Malla and others the reign of Prithvi Narayan Shah. Bahadur Shah added the copper roof in 1793.
architecture: West-facing pagoda temple of traditional brick and carved timber with a copper roof installed in 1793. Pairs of metal and stone lions guard the main door; two female figures holding vermilion flank the main stair. Ashtamatrika sculptures are kept inside.
short: Pagoda temple of the goddess Bhairavi just south of Nuwakot's seven-storey palace, home of the Sindure Jatra.
story: Walk about two hundred metres south of the seven-storey palace and you reach the temple of the goddess Bhairavi, consort of Bhairav. People here also call her Gandaki Bhairavi, after the Trishuli Gandaki river flowing far below. Face the main door: it opens to the west. Two pairs of lions guard it, one cast in metal and one carved in stone, and on either side of the stair stand two women with their hands full of sindur, red vermilion. That is a clue to the temple's great festival, the Sindure Jatra, when the crowd smears one another red. Look up at the copper roof. Bahadur Shah fixed it in 1793 and, in the same year, placed a copper plate here announcing Nepal's victory over Tibet and China, storing captured weapons on the upper floor. The 2015 earthquake devastated this temple, and you are seeing it after restoration finished in August 2020.
legend: The temple's priest, called the Dhami, was traditionally forbidden to cross the Trishuli and Tadi rivers without the king's permission; when he dies, his eldest son takes his place.
facts: The temple lies about 200 m south of the seven-storey Nuwakot Palace.
In 1793 Bahadur Shah installed a copper plate here declaring Nepal's victory in the Sino-Nepalese War, and stored captured weapons on the second storey.
The current copper roof was installed by Bahadur Shah in 1793.
The main door faces west and is guarded by a metal pair and a stone pair of lions.
Devastated by the April 2015 earthquake, the temple was restored in August 2020.

visit.hours_note: Active temple; no official hours found in sources.
visit.fee_note: No published entry fee found in the sources consulted.

earthquake_2015: The April 2015 earthquake devastated the temple; restoration was completed in August 2020.

festivals.name: Sindure Jatra (Bhairavi Jatra)
festivals.note: Procession to the Taleju temple in which participants smear each other with vermilion; animal sacrifices are offered.
festivals.note_np: तलेजु मन्दिरसम्म जुलुस निस्कन्छ, जसमा सहभागीहरूले एकअर्कालाई सिन्दूर दल्छन्; पशुबलि चढाइन्छ।

quiz.q: Which goddess is worshipped at this Nuwakot temple?
quiz.explanation: The temple is dedicated to Bhairavi, consort of Bhairav.
quiz.q_np: नुवाकोटको यस मन्दिरमा कुन देवीको पूजा गरिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: मन्दिर भैरवको शक्ति भैरवीलाई समर्पित छ।

quiz.q: What is smeared on people during the temple's main festival?
quiz.explanation: The Sindure Jatra is named after sindur, the red vermilion powder.
quiz.q_np: मन्दिरको मुख्य पर्वमा मानिसहरूलाई के दलिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: सिन्दुरे जात्राको नाम रातो अबिर सिन्दूरबाट रहेको हो।

quiz.q: Which direction does the main door face?
quiz.explanation: The main door of the temple faces west.
quiz.q_np: मुख्य ढोका कुन दिशातर्फ फर्केको छ?
quiz.explanation_np: मन्दिरको मुख्य ढोका पश्चिमतर्फ फर्केको छ।

quiz.q: Who installed the temple's copper roof in 1793?
quiz.explanation: Bahadur Shah installed the roof and a victory copper plate in 1793.
quiz.q_np: सन् 1793 मा मन्दिरमा तामाको छाना कसले राखे?
quiz.explanation_np: बहादुर शाहले सन् 1793 मा छाना र विजयको तामापत्र राखेका थिए।

quiz.q: What is the temple's hereditary priest called?
quiz.explanation: The priest is called the Dhami, and the post passes to his eldest son.
quiz.q_np: मन्दिरको वंशानुगत पुजारीलाई के भनिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: पुजारीलाई धामी भनिन्छ, र यो पद जेठो छोरालाई सर्छ।

clues: Two stone women hold red powder beside my steps, and every spring the crowd turns red in my honour.
A copper plate announcing a victory over Tibet was fixed to my walls, and captured weapons were stored upstairs.

model.notes: Squat two-roof pagoda with wide dark eaves edged in red, gilded finial, and lion pairs on a low walled courtyard.

short_np: नुवाकोटको सात तले दरबारको ठीक दक्षिणमा रहेको भैरवी देवीको पगोडा मन्दिर, सिन्दुरे जात्राको थलो।
story_np: सात तले दरबारबाट करिब दुई सय मिटर दक्षिणतिर हिँड्नुभयो भने तपाईं भैरवका शक्ति भैरवी देवीको मन्दिरमा पुग्नुहुन्छ। यहाँका मानिसहरू धेरै तल बग्ने त्रिशूली गण्डकी नदीका नाममा उनलाई गण्डकी भैरवी पनि भन्छन्। मुख्य ढोकातिर फर्कनुहोस्: त्यो पश्चिमतर्फ खुल्छ। दुई जोडी सिंहले यसको रक्षा गर्छन्, एक जोडी धातुको र एक जोडी ढुङ्गाको, र सिँढीका दुवैतिर सिन्दुर, अर्थात् रातो अबिरले हात भरिएका दुई महिला उभिएका छन्। यो मन्दिरको महान् पर्व सिन्दुरे जात्राको सङ्केत हो, जब भीडले एकअर्कालाई रातो पोतिदिन्छ। माथि तामाको छानातिर हेर्नुहोस्। बहादुर शाहले 1793 मा यसलाई मर्मत गरे र त्यही वर्ष तिब्बत र चीनमाथि नेपालको विजय घोषणा गर्ने तामाको पाता यहाँ राखे, र कब्जा गरिएका हतियार माथिल्लो तल्लामा भण्डारण गरे। 2015 को भूकम्पले यो मन्दिर ध्वस्त पार्‍यो, र अगस्ट 2020 मा पुनर्स्थापना सकिएपछिको रूपमा तपाईं यसलाई हेर्दै हुनुहुन्छ।
legend_np: यस मन्दिरका पुजारी, धामी भनिने, परम्परागत रूपमा राजाको अनुमति बिना त्रिशूली र ताडी नदी पार गर्न निषेधित थिए; उनको मृत्यु भएपछि उनको जेठो छोराले उनको ठाउँ लिन्छ।
facts_np: मन्दिर सात तले नुवाकोट दरबारबाट करिब 200 मिटर दक्षिणमा छ।
1793 मा बहादुर शाहले यहाँ नेपाल-चीन युद्धमा नेपालको विजय घोषणा गर्ने तामाको पाता राखे, र कब्जा गरिएका हतियार दोस्रो तल्लामा भण्डारण गरे।
हालको तामाको छाना बहादुर शाहले 1793 मा राखेका थिए।
मुख्य ढोका पश्चिमतर्फ फर्केको छ र धातुको एक जोडी तथा ढुङ्गाको एक जोडी सिंहले रक्षा गरेका छन्।
2015 अप्रिलको भूकम्पले ध्वस्त भएको मन्दिर अगस्ट 2020 मा पुनर्स्थापना गरियो।
quake_np: सन् 2015 अप्रिलको भूकम्पले मन्दिरलाई ध्वस्त बनायो; पुनर्स्थापना अगस्ट 2020 मा सम्पन्न भयो।
clues_np: मेरो भ्याङ्गछेउ दुई ढुङ्गाका महिलाले रातो अबिर बोकेका छन्, र हरेक वसन्तमा मेरो सम्मानमा भीड रातो हुन्छ।
तिब्बतमाथि विजयको घोषणा गर्ने तामापत्र मेरा भित्तामा ठोकियो, र कब्जा गरिएका हतियार माथिल्लो तलामा राखिए।

name: Gosaikunda
built_century_text: Natural alpine lake revered since ancient times; the Gosaikunda lake complex was designated a Ramsar wetland on 29 September 2007.
architecture: Glacial lake of 13.8 ha at 4,380 m in Langtang National Park, one of a group of lakes covering 1,030 ha. Small stone shrines and cairns stand on its shore; it is frozen for about six months a year.
short: Sacred high-altitude lake at 4,380 m, said to have been made by Shiva's trident, where thousands bathe at Janai Purnima.
story: Catch your breath. You are at 4,380 metres, beside the sacred lake of Gosaikunda in Langtang National Park. Hindus say that when the gods churned the ocean, Shiva swallowed a deadly poison to save the world. His throat burned, so he thrust his trident into this mountainside, and cold water gushed out to form the lake in front of you. Look at the stillness of the water and the bare rock around it. For roughly six months each winter the surface freezes solid. In August, on the full moon of Janai Purnima, the shore fills with thousands of pilgrims who walk two or three days up from Dhunche to bathe here and carry the water home. Down in Patan, people believe the pond at Kumbheshwar is fed by this same lake. Since 2007 the lakes around you have been protected as a Ramsar wetland of international importance.
legend: During the churning of the ocean (Samudra Manthan) Shiva swallowed poison; to cool his burning throat he struck the mountain with his trident, and the water that sprang out formed Gosaikunda.
facts: The lake lies at 4,380 m and has a surface area of 13.8 ha.
The Gosaikunda lake complex, 1,030 ha in size, was designated a Ramsar site on 29 September 2007.
The lake stays frozen for about six months in winter.
Legend says the spring feeding the Kumbheshwar pond in Patan is connected to Gosaikunda.
Among Newars the lake is called Silu, the subject of a well-known song and film.

visit.hours_note: Open-air site reached by a 2-3 day trek from Dhunche; best visited outside the frozen winter months.
visit.fee_note: Langtang National Park entry fee: foreigners NPR 3,000 and SAARC NPR 1,500 (plus 13% VAT); Nepali citizens free per most sources.

festivals.name: Janai Purnima
festivals.note: Around 10,000 pilgrims bathe in the lake on the Shrawan full moon and take its water home.
festivals.note_np: श्रावणको पूर्णिमामा करिब 10,000 तीर्थयात्री तालमा स्नान गर्छन् र त्यसको पानी घर लैजान्छन्।

quiz.q: Which god is said to have created Gosaikunda?
quiz.explanation: Legend says Shiva struck the mountain with his trident to get water after swallowing poison.
quiz.q_np: गोसाइँकुण्ड कुन देवताले बनाएको भनिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: किंवदन्ती अनुसार विष खाएपछि शिवले पानी निकाल्न त्रिशूलले पहाडमा प्रहार गरे।

quiz.q: At about what altitude does Gosaikunda lie?
quiz.explanation: The lake is at 4,380 m in Langtang National Park.

short_np: 4,380 मिटरमा रहेको पवित्र उच्च हिमाली ताल, शिवको त्रिशूलले बनाएको भनिने, जहाँ जनै पूर्णिमामा हजारौँले स्नान गर्छन्।
story_np: सास फेर्नुहोस्। तपाईं 4,380 मिटरमा, लाङटाङ राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जभित्रको पवित्र ताल गोसाइँकुण्डको छेउमा हुनुहुन्छ। हिन्दूहरू भन्छन् कि देवताहरूले समुद्र मन्थन गर्दा शिवले संसार बचाउन घातक विष निले। उनको घाँटी पोल्यो, त्यसैले उनले यही पहाडमा आफ्नो त्रिशूल रोपे, र चिसो पानी बाहिर उत्पन्न भएर तपाईंको अगाडिको ताल बन्यो। पानीको शान्तता र वरिपरिको नाङ्गो चट्टान हेर्नुहोस्। हरेक जाडोमा करिब छ महिनासम्म सतह ठोस जम्छ। अगस्टमा, जनै पूर्णिमाको दिन किनार हजारौँ तीर्थयात्रीले भरिन्छ, जो धुन्चेबाट दुई-तीन दिन हिँडेर माथि आउँछन्, यहाँ नुहाउन र पानी घरसम्म लैजान। तल पाटनमा मानिसहरू विश्वास गर्छन् कि कुम्भेश्वरको पोखरी यही तालबाट भरिन्छ। सन् 2007 देखि तपाईंको वरिपरिका तालहरू अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय महत्त्वको रामसार सिमसारका रूपमा संरक्षित छन्।
legend_np: समुद्र मन्थनका बेला शिवले विष निले; आफ्नो पोलिरहेको घाँटी चिसो पार्न उनले त्रिशूलले पहाडमा प्रहार गरे, र निस्केको पानीले गोसाइँकुण्ड बन्यो।
facts_np: ताल 4,380 मिटरमा छ र यसको सतह क्षेत्रफल 13.8 हेक्टर छ।
1,030 हेक्टरको गोसाइँकुण्ड ताल क्षेत्र सन् 2007 को सेप्टेम्बर 29 मा रामसार स्थल घोषित भयो।
जाडोमा ताल करिब छ महिनासम्म जमेको रहन्छ।
किंवदन्ती अनुसार पाटनको कुम्भेश्वर पोखरीलाई पानी दिने मुहान गोसाइँकुण्डसँग जोडिएको छ।
नेवारहरूका बीच यो तालाई सिलु भनिन्छ, जुन एउटा प्रसिद्ध गीत र चलचित्रको विषय हो।
clues_np: घाँटी पोलेका एक देवताले यस पहाडमा त्रिशूलले प्रहार गरे, र चिसो पानी बाहिर बगेर आयो।
वर्षको आधा समय म जमेको हुन्छु; अगस्टको एक पूर्णिमामा हजारौँ मानिस मलाई नुहाउन दिनौँ हिँडेर चढ्छन्।

name: Dolakha Bhimsen Temple
coord_source: Wikidata Q19679215 (P625, precision about 0.001 deg); not mapped as a named object in OpenStreetMap
built_century_text: Founding date unknown; an inscription dated 1611 AD records a renovation of the temple.
architecture: Roofless shrine: the triangular black stone idol sits open to the sky inside a walled brick-and-stone enclosure entered through a metal grille gate flanked by stone guardian figures, with a tall pillar topped by a statue rising behind the gate.
short: Roofless Newar shrine in old Dolakha bazaar whose triangular stone idol of Bhimsen is said to sweat before national disasters.
story: Step through the grille gate in old Dolakha bazaar and look up: there is no roof. The idol of Bhimsen, called Bhindyo by the Newars of this town, sits open to the sky, a triangular block of black stone. Traders pray to him for good business, and around five thousand people come every week. Devotees say the stone shows three faces in a day: Bhimeshwor in the morning, Mahadev through the day and Narayan in the evening. Local legend says twelve porters once built a cooking fire against this stone; their rice would not cook, and when one hit the stone with his ladle, it bled milk mixed with blood. The idol is famous for sweating. Drops reportedly appeared before the 1934 earthquake and before the 2001 royal massacre, and the priest would soak the sweat in cotton and send it to the palace, which replied with offerings to turn away misfortune.
legend: Twelve porters used the triangular stone as part of their cooking stove. Their rice stayed raw where it touched the stone; one porter struck it with his ladle, the stone cracked and bled blood-coated milk, and they realised it was Bhimsen.
facts: The temple is roofless; the triangular stone idol stands open to the sky.
An inscription dated 1611 AD records a renovation of the temple; its founding date is unknown.
The idol is believed to appear as Bhimeshwor in the morning, Mahadev by day and Narayan in the evening.
Sweating of the idol is read as a bad omen; it was reported in 1934, before the 2001 royal massacre and on 20 February 2020.
The temple draws around 5,000 worshippers every week.

quiz.explanation_np: मूर्ति छाना नभएको, आकाशतर्फ खुला मन्दिरमा रहेको छ।

quiz.q: Bhimsen is especially worshipped here as the god of what?
quiz.explanation: Bhindyo is the patron god of trade, commerce and fortune for the Newar business community.
quiz.q_np: यहाँ भीमसेनलाई विशेष गरी कुन कुराका देवताका रूपमा पूजा गरिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: भिन्द्योलाई नेवार व्यापारी समुदायका लागि व्यापार, वाणिज्य र भाग्यका संरक्षक देवता मानिन्छ।

quiz.q: What shape is the stone idol?
quiz.explanation: The idol is a triangular-shaped black stone.
quiz.q_np: ढुङ्गाको मूर्ति कुन आकारको छ?
quiz.explanation_np: मूर्ति त्रिकोणाकार कालो ढुङ्गा हो।

quiz.q: What is believed to happen to the idol before a national disaster?
quiz.explanation: Drops of sweat on the idol are read as a warning, e.g. before the 1934 earthquake.
quiz.q_np: राष्ट्रिय विपत्तिअघि मूर्तिलाई के हुने विश्वास गरिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: मूर्तिमा देखिने पसिनाका थोपालाई चेतावनी मानिन्छ, जस्तै 1934 को भूकम्पअघि।

quiz.q: An inscription records a renovation of the temple in which year?
quiz.explanation: An inscription dated 1611 AD mentions the renovation.
quiz.q_np: एउटा शिलालेखले मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार कुन वर्षमा भएको उल्लेख गर्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: 1611 AD को शिलालेखमा जीर्णोद्धारको उल्लेख छ।

When drops of sweat appear on my black three-cornered stone, the whole country worries.

short_np: पुरानो दोलखा बजारको छानारहित नेवारी मन्दिर, जसको त्रिकोणाकार ढुङ्गाको भीमसेनको मूर्तिले राष्ट्रिय विपत्तिअघि पसिना आउँछ भनिन्छ।
story_np: पुरानो दोलखा बजारको जालीदार ढोकाबाट प्रवेश गर्नुहोस् र माथि हेर्नुहोस्: छाना छैन। यहाँका नेवारहरूले भिन्द्यो भन्ने भीमसेनको मूर्ति कालो ढुङ्गाको त्रिकोणाकार खण्डका रूपमा खुला आकाशमुनि बसेको छ। व्यापारीहरू राम्रो व्यापारका लागि उनको प्रार्थना गर्छन्, र हरेक हप्ता करिब पाँच हजार मानिस आउँछन्। भक्तजनहरू भन्छन् ढुङ्गाले एक दिनमा तीन मुहार देखाउँछ: बिहान भीमेश्वर, दिनभर महादेव र साँझ नारायण। स्थानीय कथाअनुसार बाह्र भरियाले एक पटक यही ढुङ्गाको सहारामा खाना पकाउने आगो बालेका थिए; उनीहरूको भात पाकेन, र एकजनाले डल्लाले ढुङ्गामा हिर्काउँदा, त्यसले रगत मिसिएको दूध बगायो। यो मूर्ति पसिना आउनका लागि प्रसिद्ध छ। सन् १९३४ को भूकम्पअघि र सन् २००१ को शाही हत्याकाण्डअघि थोपा देखिएको बताइन्छ, र पुजारीले पसिना कपासमा सोसेर दरबारमा पठाउँथे, जसले दुर्भाग्य टार्न भेटीसहित जवाफ दिन्थ्यो।
legend_np: बाह्र भरियाले त्रिकोणाकार ढुङ्गालाई चुलोको भागका रूपमा प्रयोग गरे। ढुङ्गा छोएको ठाउँमा उनीहरूको भात काँचै रह्यो; एकजना भरियाले डल्लाले हिर्काए, ढुङ्गा चर्कियो र रगतले लपेटिएको दूध बग्यो, र उनीहरूले बुझे कि त्यो भीमसेन हो।
facts_np: मन्दिरमा छाना छैन; त्रिकोणाकार ढुङ्गाको मूर्ति खुला आकाशमुनि उभिएको छ।
सन् १६११ को एउटा शिलालेखले मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार अभिलेख गरेको छ; यसको स्थापनाको मिति अज्ञात छ।
मूर्ति बिहान भीमेश्वर, दिनमा महादेव र साँझ नारायणको रूपमा देखा पर्छ भन्ने विश्वास गरिन्छ।
मूर्तिबाट पसिना आउनुलाई अशुभ सङ्केत मानिन्छ; यो सन् १९३४ मा, सन् २००१ को शाही हत्याकाण्डअघि र २० फेब्रुअरी २०२० मा देखिएको बताइएको थियो।
मन्दिरमा हरेक हप्ता करिब ५,००० भक्तजन आउँछन्।
clues_np: मेरा देवता टाउकोमाथि छाना बिना बस्छन्, र व्यापारीहरू सौदाअघि उनीसँग प्रार्थना गर्छन्।
मेरो कालो त्रिकोणाकार ढुङ्गामा पसिनाका थोपा देखिँदा सारा देश चिन्तित हुन्छ।

name: Kalinchowk Bhagawati Temple
built_century_text: Founding date not documented in the sources consulted; a cable car from Kuri village was added in 2018.
architecture: Open-air summit shrine at 3,842 m: a small low enclosure crowded with iron tridents, bells and layers of prayer flags and cloth offerings, with a holy pond inside the temple area. Reached by stone steps from Kuri village or by cable car.
short: Hilltop shrine of the goddess Bhagawati at 3,842 m in Dolakha, crowded with tridents, bells and prayer flags.
story: You are standing at 3,842 metres, on the summit of Kalinchowk in Dolakha, and the shrine of the goddess Bhagawati is right in front of you. There is no grand building here. Instead, look at the forest of black iron tridents, the bells, and the thick layers of red, yellow and blue flags that devotees have tied around the goddess. This hilltop lies in the Gaurishankar Conservation Area, near the sources of the Sun Koshi and Tamakoshi rivers. For generations pilgrims climbed up from Kuri village on foot, an hour and a half of stone steps. Since 2018 a cable car does the climb in minutes, and in winter the slopes turn white and people come to play in the snow. On a clear day, turn around: the snow peaks of Gaurishankar and the Jugal and Ganesh ranges line the horizon. At Dashain and Janai Purnima the summit is packed with worshippers.
facts: The shrine stands at 3,842 m in ward 1 of Kalinchowk Rural Municipality, Dolakha.
It lies in the Gaurishankar Conservation Area, near where the Sun Koshi and Tamakoshi rivers are sourced.
A cable car from Kuri village opened in 2018; walking up takes about an hour and a half.
In winter the area is popular for snow, skiing and views of Gaurishankar, Jugal and Ganesh Himal.

visit.fee_note: No temple entry fee found in sources; the area lies in Gaurishankar Conservation Area, whose fees were not verified.

quiz.explanation_np: यो मन्दिर कालिञ्चोक भगवतीलाई समर्पित छ।

quiz.q: In which district is Kalinchowk?

quiz.q: In which year did the cable car to Kalinchowk open?

quiz.q_np: कालिञ्चोकको केबुलकार कुन वर्षमा सञ्चालनमा आयो?
quiz.explanation_np: बढ्दो आगन्तुकका लागि 2018 मा केबुलकार थपियो।

quiz.q: About how high is the shrine?
quiz.explanation: The shrine is at 3,842 m above sea level.
quiz.q_np: मन्दिर करिब कति उचाइमा छ?
quiz.explanation_np: मन्दिर समुद्र सतहभन्दा 3,842 मि. उचाइमा छ।

quiz.q: Kalinchowk lies inside which protected area?
quiz.explanation: It is part of the Gaurishankar Conservation Area.
quiz.q_np: कालिञ्चोक कुन संरक्षित क्षेत्रभित्र पर्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: यो गौरीशङ्कर संरक्षण क्षेत्रको भाग हो।

Pilgrims once climbed for hours from Kuri village; since 2018 a cable lifts them up in minutes.

story_np: तपाईं दोलखाको कालिञ्चोकको शिखरमा ३,८४२ मिटरको उचाइमा हुनुहुन्छ, र देवी भगवतीको मन्दिर ठीक तपाईंको अगाडि छ। यहाँ कुनै भव्य भवन छैन। बरु, कालो फलामका त्रिशूलहरूको जङ्गल, घण्टहरू, र भक्तजनहरूले देवीको वरिपरि बाँधेका रातो, पहेँलो र निलो झन्डाका बाक्ला तहहरू हेर्नुहोस्। यो डाँडो गौरीशङ्कर संरक्षण क्षेत्रमा पर्छ, सुनकोशी र तामाकोशी नदीका स्रोतहरू नजिक। पुस्तौँदेखि तीर्थयात्रीहरू कुरी गाउँबाट पैदल उक्लन्थे, ढुङ्गाका भर्‍याङमा डेढ घण्टा। सन् २०१८ देखि केबल कारले त्यो चढाइ केही मिनेटमा गर्छ, र जाडोमा भिरालाहरू सेता हुन्छन् र मानिसहरू हिउँमा खेल्न आउँछन्। स्वच्छ दिनमा, फर्केर हेर्नुहोस्: गौरीशङ्कर र जुगल र गणेश हिमालका हिउँले ढाकिएका चुचुराहरू क्षितिजमा पङ्क्तिबद्ध छन्। दशैँ र जनै पूर्णिमामा शिखर भक्तजनहरूले भरिन्छ।
facts_np: मन्दिर दोलखाको कालिञ्चोक गाउँपालिका वडा १ मा ३,८४२ मिटरमा छ।
यो गौरीशङ्कर संरक्षण क्षेत्रमा, सुनकोशी र तामाकोशी नदीको उद्गम नजिक पर्छ।
कुरी गाउँबाट केबल कार सन् २०१८ मा सञ्चालनमा आयो; हिँडेर चढ्न करिब डेढ घण्टा लाग्छ।
जाडोमा यो क्षेत्र हिउँ, स्कीइङ र गौरीशङ्कर, जुगल र गणेश हिमालको दृश्यका लागि लोकप्रिय छ।
clues_np: न छाना, न मीनार: 3,800 मि. नजिकको हिमाली शिखरमा फलामका त्रिशूलको झुण्ड र फहराइरहेका कपडा मात्र।
तीर्थयात्रीहरू पहिले कुरी गाउँबाट घण्टौँ हिँडेर चढ्थे; 2018 देखि केबुलले मिनेटमै माथि पुर्‍याउँछ।

built_century_text: Date of construction not documented in the sources consulted; the stupa is said to hold the bone relics of Prince Mahasattva, an earlier incarnation of the Buddha.
architecture: Whitewashed dome stupa on a square stepped base with a gilded spire and Buddha eyes, surrounded by smaller white chaityas and strings of prayer flags. A stairway leads up to the Thrangu Tashi Yangtse (Namo Buddha) Monastery on the hilltop.
short: Stupa marking where a prince, an earlier life of the Buddha, gave his body to feed a starving tigress and her cubs.
story: You are at Namo Buddha, 52 kilometres south-east of Kathmandu, and this white stupa holds one of the most moving stories in Buddhism. Long ago, a prince named Mahasattva, an earlier life of the Buddha, walked these hills with his brothers. They came upon a tigress so weak from hunger that she could not feed her cubs. Out of compassion, the prince offered his own body so they could live. The stupa in front of you is said to hold his bone relics, and the name means homage to the Buddha. Walk clockwise around it under the prayer flags, past the smaller white chaityas. Then climb the stairway into the woods. Up there, beside the large Thrangu Tashi Yangtse monastery, is the spot where the prince is said to have been eaten, with a carving of the tigress and her cubs. Pilgrims of every Tibetan Buddhist tradition still come here.
legend: Prince Mahasattva, an earlier incarnation of Shakyamuni Buddha, found a starving tigress unable to feed her cubs and gave his own body to save them; the stupa is said to enshrine his bone relics.
facts: Namo Buddha lies about 52 km south-east of Kathmandu in Kavrepalanchok District.
The stupa is said to house the bone relics of Prince Mahasattva.
It is considered one of the three most important stupas and pilgrimage sites around the Kathmandu Valley.
The Karma Kagyu Thrangu Tashi Yangtse Monastery stands on the hill above the stupa.
In Tibetan the site is called Takmo Lujin, meaning 'tigress body-gift'.

short_np: भोकले मरन लागेकी बाघिनी र उनका बच्चालाई आफ्नो शरीर दिने राजकुमार, बुद्धको पूर्वजन्म, को स्मारक स्तूप।
story_np: तपाईं काठमाडौँबाट 52 किलोमिटर दक्षिणपूर्वमा रहेको नमोबुद्धमा हुनुहुन्छ, र यो सेतो स्तूपले बौद्ध धर्मको सबैभन्दा मार्मिक कथाहरूमध्ये एक सम्हालेको छ। धेरै पहिले, महासत्त्व नामका राजकुमार, बुद्धको पूर्वजन्म, आफ्ना दाजुभाइसँग यी डाँडामा हिँडे। उनीहरूले एउटी बाघिनी भेटे, जो भोकले यति कमजोर थिई कि उसले आफ्ना बच्चालाई दूध खुवाउन सक्दैनथी। करुणाले गर्दा राजकुमारले आफ्नो शरीर अर्पण गरे ताकि तिनीहरू बाँच्न सकून्। तपाईंको अगाडिको स्तूपमा उनका अस्थि अवशेष रहेको भनिन्छ, र नामको अर्थ बुद्धलाई नमन हो। प्रार्थना झण्डामुनि, साना सेता चैत्यहरू पार गर्दै यसलाई घडीको दिशामा परिक्रमा गर्नुहोस्। अनि सिँढी चढेर जङ्गलमा जानुहोस्। माथि, विशाल थ्राङ्गु ताशी याङ्त्से गुम्बाको छेउमा, राजकुमार खाइएको भनिने ठाउँ छ, जहाँ बाघिनी र उनका बच्चाको नक्काशी छ। हरेक तिब्बती बौद्ध परम्पराका तीर्थयात्री अझै यहाँ आउँछन्।
legend_np: शाक्यमुनि बुद्धका पूर्व अवतार राजकुमार महासत्त्वले भोकले आतुर, बच्चालाई खुवाउन नसक्ने एउटी बाघिनी भेटे र तिनीहरूलाई बचाउन आफ्नो शरीर दिए; स्तूपमा उनका अस्थि अवशेष राखिएको भनिन्छ।
facts_np: नमोबुद्ध काठमाडौँबाट करिब 52 किलोमिटर दक्षिणपूर्व, काभ्रेपलाञ्चोक जिल्लामा छ।
स्तूपमा राजकुमार महासत्त्वका अस्थि अवशेष रहेको भनिन्छ।
यो काठमाडौँ उपत्यकावरिपरिका तीन सबैभन्दा महत्त्वपूर्ण स्तूप र तीर्थस्थलमध्ये एक मानिन्छ।
कर्मा कग्यु थ्राङ्गु ताशी याङ्त्से गुम्बा स्तूपमाथिको डाँडामा छ।
तिब्बतीमा यो स्थललाई टक्मो लुजिन भनिन्छ, जसको अर्थ 'बाघिनीलाई शरीर-दान' हो।
clues_np: एक राजकुमारले धर्काहरू भएकी भोकी आमा बिरालीलाई देखे र आफूसँग भएको एक मात्र खाना दिए: आफैँलाई।
तिब्बतीमा मेरो नामको अर्थ ‘बाघिनीलाई शरीर दान’ हो; मेरो सेतो गुम्बजमा उदार राजकुमारको अस्थि राखिएको भनिन्छ।

name: Indreshwar Mahadev Temple
built_century_text: First built over a lingam in 1294, often called the oldest surviving temple in Nepal; Lonely Planet notes the present shrine dates mainly from the 15th century.
architecture: Three-tiered Newar pagoda of brick and carved timber on a stepped stone plinth, one of the largest and tallest pagoda temples in Nepal. The roof struts of the two lower storeys carry fine woodcarving, and the upper section is hung with pots and pans offered by newly-wed couples.
short: Three-roofed Shiva pagoda in Panauti, first built in 1294 and often called Nepal's oldest surviving temple.
story: Welcome to Panauti, an old trading town on the salt route between Tibet and India, and to its great temple of Indreshwar Mahadev. You are looking at one of the largest and tallest pagoda temples in Nepal, three roofs high. A temple was first raised on this spot over a Shiva lingam in 1294, which is why many call it the oldest surviving temple in the country. Walk slowly around it and study the roof struts on the lower two storeys; their carving is among the finest Newar woodwork anywhere. Now look higher. See the pots and pans hanging from the upper roof? They were offered by young married couples hoping for a happy, prosperous home. Facing the door, a stone bull, Nandi, waits for his master. This temple came through the 2015 earthquake in good condition. Every twelve years in Magh, the town's Makar Mela fills the river confluence nearby with pilgrims.
legend: Local tradition holds that Shiva created the lingam here himself; the hidden 'third river' of Panauti is said to begin at this temple and flow to the confluence below.
facts: The temple was first built over a lingam in 1294.
It is one of the largest and tallest pagoda temples in Nepal, with three roofs.
Pots and pans hung on the upper storey are offerings from young married couples.
Panauti's medieval complex was placed on Nepal's UNESCO Tentative List in 1996.
The temple survived the 2015 earthquake in good condition.

short_np: पनौतीको तीन छाने शिव पगोडा, सन् 1294 मा पहिलो पटक बनेको र प्रायः नेपालको सबैभन्दा पुरानो बाँचेको मन्दिर भनिने।
story_np: तिब्बत र भारतबीचको नुन बाटोमा पर्ने पुरानो व्यापारिक सहर पनौतीमा र यसको ठूलो इन्द्रेश्वर महादेव मन्दिरमा स्वागत छ। तपाईं नेपालको सबैभन्दा ठूला र अग्ला पगोडा मन्दिरमध्ये एक हेर्दै हुनुहुन्छ, तीन छाना अग्लो। यही ठाउँमा सन् 1294 मा शिवलिङ्गमाथि पहिलो पटक मन्दिर उठाइएको थियो, त्यसैले धेरैले यसलाई देशको सबैभन्दा पुरानो बाँचेको मन्दिर भन्छन्। यसको वरिपरि बिस्तारै हिँड्नुहोस् र तल्ला दुई तलाका छानाका टेकाहरू ध्यानले हेर्नुहोस्; यसको कुँदाइ जहीँ पनि पाइने उत्कृष्ट नेवार काष्ठकलामध्ये हो। अब माथि हेर्नुहोस्। माथिल्लो छानामा झुण्डिएका भाँडाकुँडा देख्नुभयो? ती खुसी र समृद्ध घरको आशा गर्ने नवविवाहित जोडीहरूले चढाएका हुन्। ढोकाको सामु ढुङ्गाको साँढे, नन्दी, आफ्ना स्वामीको प्रतीक्षा गर्दैछ। यो मन्दिर सन् 2015 को भूकम्पबाट राम्रो अवस्थामा बाँच्यो। हरेक बाह्र वर्षमा माघमा लाग्ने पनौतीको मकर मेलाले नजिकैको नदी सङ्गमलाई तीर्थयात्रीले भरिदिन्छ।
legend_np: स्थानीय परम्परा अनुसार शिवले आफैँ यहाँ लिङ्ग सिर्जना गरे; पनौतीको लुकेको ‘तेस्रो नदी’ यही मन्दिरबाट सुरु भई तलको सङ्गमसम्म बग्छ भनिन्छ।
facts_np: मन्दिर पहिलो पटक सन् 1294 मा लिङ्गमाथि बनाइएको थियो।
यो तीन छाना भएको नेपालको सबैभन्दा ठूला र अग्ला पगोडा मन्दिरमध्ये एक हो।
माथिल्लो तलामा झुण्ड्याइएका भाँडाकुँडा नवविवाहित जोडीहरूले चढाएका भेटी हुन्।

name: Chandeshwori Temple
deity: Chandeshwori (form of Parvati, slayer of the demon Chanda)
built_century_text: Believed to have been built in the 17th century; the story of the goddess is told in the Nepal Mahatmya of the Skanda Purana.
architecture: Three-roofed pagoda with gilded metal roofs and carved struts, set in a stone-paved courtyard with stone pillars, small shikhara shrines and a lingam shrine in front. A mural shows the goddess slaying Chanda, and a wall painting of Bhairav is said to be the largest in Nepal Mandala.
short: Three-roofed golden pagoda above Banepa where the goddess is said to have killed the demon Chanda.
story: Follow the lane about a kilometre north-east of Banepa town, along the Punyamata river, and the golden roofs of Chandeshwori rise from the forest edge. This temple, believed to date from the 17th century, honours the mother goddess who defeated the demon Chanda. Shiva had given Chanda a boon that only a woman could kill him, and he terrorised the world. The gods hid in this forest as birds, and the goddess slipped into a tree. When Chanda cut the tree down, she burst out on a great lion and slew him. From the belly of the demon, a devotee of Shiva, a lingam grew; you can see it in the small shrine just in front of the main temple. Now find the huge painting of Bhairav on one of the walls, said to be the largest in the old Nepal Mandala. Locals say the rocks by the river still bear marks of the battle.
legend: The demon Chanda could be killed only by a woman. Hiding in the Banepa forest, the mother goddess emerged from a tree he cut down, rode out on a lion and killed him; a Shiva lingam grew from his belly, now in the shrine before the temple.
facts: The temple lies about 1 km north-east of Banepa along the Punyamata river.
It is believed to have been built in the 17th century.
A mural shows Chandeshwori slaying the demon Chanda.
A painting of Bhairav on one wall is said to be the largest in the Nepal Mandala.
The lingam in the small shrine in front is said to have grown from the demon's belly.

short_np: बनेपामाथि रहेको तीन छाने सुनौलो पगोडा, जहाँ देवीले चण्ड दानवलाई मारेकी भनिन्छ।
story_np: बनेपा सहरको करिब एक किलोमिटर उत्तर-पूर्व, पुण्यमाता खोलाको छेउछेउको गल्लीमा लागिरहनुहोस्, र जङ्गलको किनारबाट चण्डेश्वरीका सुनौला छानाहरू उठेको देखिन्छ। १७ औं शताब्दीको मानिने यो मन्दिर चण्ड दानवलाई पराजित गर्ने मातृदेवीको सम्मानमा बनेको हो। शिवले चण्डलाई केवल नारीले मात्र मार्न सक्ने वरदान दिएका थिए, र उसले संसारलाई आतङ्कित पारेको थियो। देवताहरू चराको रूपमा यो जङ्गलमा लुके, र देवी एउटा रुखभित्र पसिन्। चण्डले रुख काटेपछि, उनी विशाल सिंहमाथि चढेर बाहिर निस्किन् र उसलाई वध गरिन्। शिवका भक्त दानवको पेटबाट शिवलिङ्ग उम्रियो; यसलाई तपाईं मुख्य मन्दिरको ठीक अगाडिको सानो मन्दिरमा देख्न सक्नुहुन्छ। अब पर्खालमा रहेको भैरवको विशाल चित्र खोज्नुहोस्, जसलाई पुरानो नेपाल मण्डलकै सबैभन्दा ठूलो भनिन्छ। स्थानीयहरू भन्छन् नदीका चट्टानहरूमा अझै युद्धका चिन्ह छन्।
legend_np: चण्ड दानवलाई केवल नारीले मात्र मार्न सक्थ्यो। बनेपाको जङ्गलमा लुकेकी मातृदेवी उसले काटेको रुखबाट निस्किन्, सिंहमा चढेर बाहिर आइन् र उसलाई मारिन्; उसको पेटबाट शिवलिङ्ग उम्रियो, जो अहिले मन्दिरको अगाडिको सानो मन्दिरमा छ।

यो १७ औं शताब्दीमा बनेको मानिन्छ।
एउटा भित्तेचित्रमा चण्डेश्वरीले चण्ड दानवको वध गरेको देखाइएको छ।

name: Palanchok Bhagawati Temple
built_century_text: Believed (by tradition) to date from the reign of the Licchavi king Manadeva (464-505 AD); not firmly documented.
architecture: Pagoda-style temple with two tiled roofs edged in red cloth frills and a tall gilded pinnacle, on a hilltop courtyard. Inside is a three-foot black stone image of the goddess with 18 arms.
short: Hilltop pagoda of the 18-armed goddess Bhagawati, revered as the elder sister of all Bhagawatis in Nepal.
story: You have climbed to the summit of Palanchok hill, 1,563 metres up, seven kilometres north of Panchkhal on the Araniko Highway. In front of you is the temple of Palanchok Bhagawati, whom devotees call the elder sister of all the Bhagawati goddesses of Nepal. Tradition says the shrine goes back to the Licchavi king Manadeva, who ruled about fifteen hundred years ago. Peer into the sanctum. The goddess is carved from black stone, only about three feet tall, yet she has eighteen arms, each ready to protect her devotees from danger and misfortune. Tuesdays and Saturdays are her special days, and at Dashain and Chaite Dashain thousands of pilgrims queue here with offerings. Now turn around. From this hilltop you can see the Himalaya stretching across the northern sky. The 2015 earthquake left the temple leaning slightly, and it spent the following years under scaffolding while repairs were carried out.
facts: The temple stands at 1,563 m on Palanchok hill, about 7 km north of Panchkhal.
Its black stone idol of the goddess is about three feet tall and has 18 arms.
Tradition dates the temple to King Manadeva (464-505 AD).
Palanchok Bhagawati is regarded as the elder sister of the other Bhagawati shrines of Nepal.
The Kshama ritual is held on the full moons of Baisakh and Jestha.

short_np: अठार हात भएकी देवी भगवतीको डाँडाको पगोडा, नेपालका सबै भगवतीकी जेठी दिदीका रूपमा पूजिने।
story_np: तपाईं पाँचखालबाट अरनिको राजमार्गमा सात किलोमिटर उत्तरमा रहेको पलाञ्चोक डाँडाको १,५६३ मिटर उचाइको शिखरमा उक्लनुभएको छ। तपाईंको अगाडि पलाञ्चोक भगवतीको मन्दिर छ, जसलाई भक्तजनहरूले नेपालका सबै भगवती देवीकी जेठी दिदी भन्छन्। परम्पराअनुसार मन्दिर करिब पन्ध्र सय वर्षअघि शासन गरेका लिच्छवि राजा मानदेवसम्म पुग्छ। गर्भगृहभित्र हेर्नुहोस्। देवी कालो ढुङ्गाबाट कुँदिएकी छिन्, करिब तीन फिट मात्र अग्ली, तर उनका अठारवटा हात छन्, हरेक भक्तजनलाई खतरा र दुर्भाग्यबाट जोगाउन तयार। मङ्गलबार र शनिबार उनका विशेष दिन हुन्, र दशैँ र चैते दशैँमा हजारौँ तीर्थयात्री भेटी लिएर यहाँ लाइन लाग्छन्। अब फर्केर हेर्नुहोस्। यो डाँडाबाट उत्तरी आकाशभरि फैलिएको हिमालय देखिन्छ। सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पले मन्दिरलाई अलिकति ढल्काएको थियो, र मर्मतसम्भार हुँदा त्यसपछिका वर्षहरू मन्दिर टेको लगाएर बित्यो।
facts_np: मन्दिर पाँचखालबाट करिब ७ किमी उत्तर, पलाञ्चोक डाँडामा १,५६३ मिटरमा छ।
देवीको कालो ढुङ्गाको मूर्ति करिब तीन फिट अग्लो छ र यसका १८ हात छन्।
परम्पराले मन्दिरलाई राजा मानदेव (४६४-५०५ ई.) सँग जोड्छ।
पलाञ्चोक भगवतीलाई नेपालका अन्य भगवती मन्दिरहरूकी जेठी दिदी मानिन्छ।
क्षमा अनुष्ठान वैशाख र जेठको पूर्णिमामा गरिन्छ।
quake_np: सन् २०१५ अप्रिलको भूकम्पले मुख्य मन्दिरलाई अलिकति ढल्कायो; सन् २०१८ मा मर्मतका लागि यो टेको लगाइएको थियो। नजिकैको कालिका भगवती मन्दिर ध्वस्त भयो।

भक्तजनहरू मेरी देवीलाई देशभरका आफ्ना नामका सबै देवीकी जेठी दिदी भन्छन्।

name: Halesi Mahadev (Halesi-Maratika Caves)
deity: Shiva (Mahadev); Padmasambhava and Mandarava for Buddhists; ancestral deity of the Kirati Rai
built_century_text: Natural cave; referred to in Himalayan literature as early as the 12th century, in the Kathang Zanglingma biography of Padmasambhava.
architecture: Natural limestone cave with an east-facing half-moon entrance, about 67 ft below the surface, round in plan with a 193 ft diameter and a second cave beneath. Shrines and railings fill the cave mouth; a Buddhist monastery stands on the hill nearby.
short: Sacred cave in Khotang revered by Hindus as Shiva's hiding place and by Buddhists as the cave of long life.
story: Go down the steps and stand at the mouth of the cave. Its entrance is shaped like a half moon and faces east, toward the morning sun. You are at Halesi, in the hills of Khotang, between the Dudh Koshi and Sun Koshi rivers, and three faiths share this cave. Hindus call it Halesi Mahadev, the Pashupatinath of the east. They say Shiva hid inside for six thousand years to escape the demon Bhasmasur, who could burn anything he touched to ash. Look for the natural stone lingam in the darkness. Buddhists know the place as Maratika, where Guru Padmasambhava and his consort Mandarava are said to have gained the power of long life, so you will see monks and a monastery on the hill above. For the Kirati Rai people it is an ancestral home, where their forefather once lived. On Shivaratri and Bala Chaturdashi the cave fills with pilgrims.
legend: Shiva hid in this cave for 6,000 years to escape the demon Bhasmasur. For Buddhists, Padmasambhava and Mandarava attained the vidyadhara of longevity here.
facts: The cave entrance is half-moon shaped and faces east.
The cave is about 67 ft below the surface and has a diameter of about 193 ft, with another cave beneath it.
It lies between the Dudh Koshi and Sun Koshi rivers, about 185 km south-west of Mount Everest.
It is mentioned in Himalayan literature as far back as the 12th century.
The Kirati Rai regard Halesi as an ancestral place of their forefather Raechhakule.

quiz.q: Which demon is Shiva said to have hidden from in the Halesi cave?
quiz.explanation: Shiva hid in the cave to escape Bhasmasur.
quiz.q_np: शिवले हलेसी गुफामा कुन दानवबाट लुकेको भनिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: शिव भस्मासुरबाट बच्न गुफामा लुकेका थिए।

quiz.q: What nickname is given to Halesi Mahadev?
quiz.explanation: The cave is nicknamed 'the Pashupatinath of the east'.
quiz.q_np: हलेसी महादेवलाई कुन उपनाम दिइन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: गुफालाई ‘पूर्वको पशुपतिनाथ’ भनिन्छ।

quiz.q: Buddhists know the cave as Maratika and link it with which master?
quiz.explanation: Padmasambhava and Mandarava are said to have attained long life here.
quiz.q_np: बौद्धहरू यो गुफालाई मरतिका भन्छन् र कुन गुरुसँग जोड्छन्?
quiz.explanation_np: पद्मसम्भव र मन्दारवाले यहाँ दीर्घायु प्राप्त गरेको भनिन्छ।

quiz.q: Which direction does the cave's half-moon entrance face?

quiz.q_np: गुफाको अर्धचन्द्राकार प्रवेशद्वार कुन दिशातर्फ फर्केको छ?
quiz.explanation_np: प्रवेशद्वार अर्धचन्द्रको आकारको छ र पूर्वतर्फ फर्केको छ।

quiz.q: Between which two rivers does Halesi lie?
quiz.explanation: The cave lies between the Dudh Koshi and Sun Koshi rivers.
quiz.q_np: हलेसी कुन दुई नदीको बीचमा पर्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: गुफा दूधकोशी र सुनकोशी नदीका बीचमा पर्छ।

clues: A god hid in my darkness for six thousand years from a demon whose touch turned everything to ash.
My mouth is a half moon facing sunrise; Hindus, Buddhists and Kirati Rai all call me sacred.

short_np: खोटाङको पवित्र गुफा, हिन्दूले शिवको लुक्ने ठाउँका रूपमा र बौद्धले दीर्घायुको गुफाका रूपमा पूज्ने।
story_np: सिँढी ओर्लेर गुफाको मुखमा उभिनुहोस्। यसको प्रवेशद्वार अर्धचन्द्रको आकारको छ र पूर्वतिर, बिहानको घामतिर, फर्केको छ। तपाईं दूधकोशी र सुनकोशी नदीको बीचमा रहेको खोटाङका डाँडामा हलेसीमा हुनुहुन्छ, र तीन धर्मले यो गुफा बाँडेका छन्। हिन्दूहरूले यसलाई हलेसी महादेव, पूर्वको पशुपतिनाथ, भन्छन्। उनीहरू भन्छन्, जे छोए पनि खरानी बनाउन सक्ने भस्मासुर दानवबाट बच्न शिव छ हजार वर्ष यहीँ भित्र लुकेका थिए। अँध्यारोमा प्राकृतिक ढुङ्गाको शिवलिङ्ग खोज्नुहोस्। बौद्धहरू यो ठाउँलाई मारातिका भन्छन्, जहाँ गुरु पद्मसम्भव र उनकी सहचरी मन्दारवाले दीर्घायुको शक्ति पाएका भनिन्छ, त्यसैले माथिको डाँडामा भिक्षुहरू र गुम्बा देख्नुहुन्छ। किराती राईहरूका लागि यो पूर्खाको घर हो, जहाँ उनीहरूका पुर्खा बसेका थिए। शिवरात्रि र बाला चतुर्दशीमा गुफा तीर्थयात्रीले भरिन्छ।
legend_np: शिव भस्मासुर दानवबाट बच्न यस गुफामा 6,000 वर्ष लुकेका थिए। बौद्धहरूका लागि, पद्मसम्भव र मन्दारवाले यहाँ दीर्घायुको विद्याधर सिद्धि प्राप्त गरे।
facts_np: गुफाको प्रवेशद्वार अर्धचन्द्राकार छ र पूर्वतिर फर्केको छ।
गुफा सतहभन्दा करिब 67 फिट तल छ र यसको व्यास करिब 193 फिट छ, यसमुनि अर्को गुफा पनि छ।
यो दूधकोशी र सुनकोशी नदीबीच, सगरमाथाबाट करिब 185 किलोमिटर दक्षिणपश्चिममा छ।
हिमालयी साहित्यमा यो बाह्रौँ शताब्दीदेखि नै उल्लेख भएको पाइन्छ।
किराती राईहरू हलेसीलाई आफ्ना पुर्खा रैछकुलेको पूर्खौली स्थान मान्छन्।
clues_np: एक देवता छ हजार वर्षसम्म मेरो अँध्यारोमा लुके, जसको स्पर्शले सबै कुरा खरानी बनाउने एक दानवबाट।
मेरो मुख सूर्योदयतिर फर्केको अर्धचन्द्र हो; हिन्दू, बौद्ध र किराँत राई सबैले मलाई पवित्र मान्छन्।

name: Pathibhara Devi Temple
deity: Pathibhara Devi (Durga); revered by Limbu people as Yuma Sammang on Mukkumlung hill
built_century_text: Ancient hilltop sacred rock revered by Limbu and Hindu devotees; the Pathibhara Area Development Committee formed in 1995, and in 2001 the rock was replaced by a statue of Durga.
architecture: Open-air hilltop shrine at 3,794 m: a richly dressed statue of the goddess under a canopy, surrounded by tridents, huge bells and lines of prayer flags, with small shelter buildings on the stony summit.
short: Shaktipeeth on a 3,794 m summit in Taplejung, sacred to Hindus as Durga and to Limbus as Mukkumlung.
story: You have reached the summit of Pathibhara, 3,794 metres up in Taplejung, a long climb north-east of Phungling bazaar. Ring one of the great bells and listen to it echo across the ridges. Long before any statue stood here, the Limbu people revered a great rock on this hilltop, and they saw the whole Mukkumlung hill as a form of their goddess Yuma Sammang. Hindus saw the same rock as Durga, and today Pathibhara is counted among the Shakti Peethas. Local legend tells of shepherds who lost hundreds of sheep on this very spot. In a dream the goddess asked them for a sacrifice and a shrine; when they obeyed, the lost flock came back. Since 2001 a statue of Durga has stood in place of the rock. Look east on a clear morning: the white wall of Kanchenjunga fills the sky. Pilgrims from across Nepal and India climb here believing she grants their wishes.
legend: Shepherds lost hundreds of sheep while grazing here. The goddess appeared in their dream and asked for a sacrifice and a shrine; when they offered it, the lost herd returned, and the custom of sacrifice at the temple began.
facts: The temple stands at 3,794 m, about 19.4 km north-east of Phungling.
Limbus revere the hill as Mukkumlung, a natural form of the goddess Yuma Sammang.
In 2001 the sacred rock on the summit was replaced with a statue of Durga.
It is one of the Shakti Peethas and a side route of the Kanchenjunga trek.
Kanchenjunga and Kumbhakarna can be seen from the temple.

visit.hours_note: Open-air summit shrine; temperatures can drop to around -2 to 1 C. No official hours found in sources.

quiz.explanation_np: मन्दिर ताप्लेजुङ जिल्लाको एउटा डाँडामा छ।

quiz.q: What did the shepherds of the legend lose?
quiz.explanation: They lost hundreds of sheep, which returned after they offered a sacrifice.
quiz.q_np: किंवदन्तीका गोठालाहरूले के गुमाएका थिए?
quiz.explanation_np: उनीहरूले सयौँ भेडा गुमाएका थिए, जुन बलि चढाएपछि फर्किए।

quiz.q: What do the Limbu people call the hill?
quiz.explanation: Limbus see the Mukkumlung hill as a form of the goddess Yuma Sammang.
quiz.q_np: लिम्बू जातिले यो डाँडालाई के भन्छन्?
quiz.explanation_np: लिम्बूहरू मुक्कुमलुङ डाँडालाई देवी युमा साम्मङको रूप मान्छन्।

quiz.explanation: The temple is at 3,794 m above sea level.
quiz.q_np: मन्दिर करिब कति उचाइमा छ?
quiz.explanation_np: मन्दिर समुद्र सतहबाट 3,794 मि. को उचाइमा छ।

quiz.q: In which year was the summit rock replaced by a statue of Durga?
quiz.explanation: The development committee replaced the sacred rock with a statue in 2001.
quiz.q_np: शिखरको चट्टानलाई दुर्गाको मूर्तिले कुन वर्ष प्रतिस्थापन गरियो?
quiz.explanation_np: विकास समितिले 2001 मा पवित्र चट्टानलाई मूर्तिले प्रतिस्थापन गर्‍यो।

clues: Shepherds' lost flock returned only after a dream-goddess was given her offering on this summit.
Limbus call this hill Mukkumlung; from its top the white wall of the world's third-highest mountain looms.

short_np: ताप्लेजुङको 3,794 मिटर टुप्पोमा रहेको शक्तिपीठ, हिन्दूका लागि दुर्गा र लिम्बूका लागि मुक्कुम्लुङका रूपमा पवित्र।
story_np: तपाईं ताप्लेजुङमा 3,794 मिटर माथि पाथीभराको टुप्पोमा पुग्नुभएको छ, फुङलिङ बजारको उत्तरपूर्वतिर लामो उकालो। एउटा ठूलो घण्ट बजाउनुहोस् र यसको गुञ्जन डाँडाहरूभर प्रतिध्वनित हुँदै गरेको सुन्नुहोस्। यहाँ कुनै मूर्ति उभिनुभन्दा धेरै पहिले लिम्बू जातिले यो डाँडाको ठूलो चट्टानलाई पूजा गर्थे, र उनीहरूले पूरै मुक्कुम्लुङ डाँडालाई आफ्नी देवी युमा साम्माङको रूप मान्थे। हिन्दूले त्यही चट्टानलाई दुर्गाका रूपमा देखे, र आज पाथीभरा शक्तिपीठहरूमध्ये गनिन्छ। स्थानीय किंवदन्तीले यही ठाउँमा सयौँ भेडा गुमाएका गोठालाहरूको कथा भन्छ। सपनामा देवीले उनीहरूसँग बलि र मन्दिर मागिन्; उनीहरूले मानेपछि हराएको बथान फर्कियो। सन् 2001 देखि चट्टानको ठाउँमा दुर्गाको मूर्ति उभिएको छ। स्पष्ट बिहान पूर्वतिर हेर्नुहोस्: कञ्चनजङ्घाको सेतो पर्खालले आकाश भरिन्छ। नेपाल र भारतभरिका तीर्थयात्रीहरू उनले आफ्ना इच्छा पूरा गर्छिन् भन्ने विश्वासमा यहाँ उक्लन्छन्।
legend_np: यहाँ चराउँदा गोठालाहरूले सयौँ भेडा गुमाए। देवी उनीहरूको सपनामा देखा परिन् र बलि तथा मन्दिर मागिन्; उनीहरूले चढाएपछि हराएको बथान फर्कियो, र मन्दिरमा बलि दिने चलन सुरु भयो।
facts_np: मन्दिर 3,794 मिटरमा, फुङलिङबाट करिब 19.4 कि.मि. उत्तरपूर्वमा छ।
लिम्बूहरूले यो डाँडालाई मुक्कुम्लुङ, देवी युमा साम्माङको प्राकृतिक रूप मानेर पूजा गर्छन्।
सन् 2001 मा टुप्पोको पवित्र चट्टानलाई दुर्गाको मूर्तिले प्रतिस्थापन गरियो।
यो शक्तिपीठहरूमध्ये एक हो र कञ्चनजङ्घा पदयात्राको एउटा शाखा बाटो हो।
मन्दिरबाट कञ्चनजङ्घा र कुम्भकर्ण देख्न सकिन्छ।
clues_np: यस शिखरमा सपनामा आएकी देवीलाई भेटी चढाएपछि मात्र गोठालाहरूका हराएका बगाल फर्किए।
लिम्बूहरू यो डाँडालाई मुक्कुमलुङ भन्छन्; यसको टुप्पोबाट संसारको तेस्रो अग्लो हिमालको सेतो पर्खाल देखिन्छ।

name: Barahachhetra
coord_source: OpenStreetMap node 3116761691 ('Bahara Chhetra'); Wikidata Q4858196 gives only 26.83, 87.18
deity: Varaha (boar incarnation of Vishnu) with Lakshmi
built_century_text: Ancient tirtha mentioned in the Brahma, Varaha and Skanda Puranas and the Mahabharata; the present main temple was rebuilt by Juddha Shumsher in 1991 BS (c. 1934-35) after the 1990 BS (1934) earthquake.
architecture: Group of whitewashed dome-roofed temples on terraces above the Saptakoshi river, including the main Varaha temple and shrines of Lakshmi, Panchayan, Guruvaraha, Suryavaraha, Kokavaraha and Nageshwar, with pilgrim rest houses. Statues over 1,500 years old have been found here.
short: One of Nepal's Char Dham: white-domed temples of Vishnu's boar incarnation where the Koka meets the Koshi.
story: Listen: below you, the mighty Saptakoshi thunders out of the hills where the Koka river joins it. You are at Barahachhetra, one of the four great pilgrimage dhams of Nepal, praised in the Puranas and even in the Mahabharata. The story says that when a demon dragged the earth down toward the underworld, Lord Vishnu took the form of Varaha, a mighty boar, and lifted her back up on his tusk. Then he rested here beside the Koshi with his wife Lakshmi. Find the large image of Varaha holding the earth. The white domed temple you see is fairly new; the 1934 earthquake brought the old one down, and Juddha Shumsher had it rebuilt. Yet statues more than fifteen hundred years old have been found around you. Limbu people call this place Mouksik Sawalung, the winter home of the god Dungdung Sammang. At Kartik Purnima and Makar Sankranti, crowds come to bathe in the river.
legend: When the earth was being dragged into Patala, Vishnu took the form of the boar Varaha and lifted her out on his tusk, then sat with Lakshmi on the bank of the Koshi; the place is named after that incarnation.
facts: Barahachhetra is one of the Char Dham (four great pilgrimage sites) of Nepal.
It lies at the confluence of the Koka and Koshi rivers in Sunsari District.
The present temple was rebuilt by Juddha Shumsher in 1991 BS after the 1990 BS (1934) earthquake.
There are nine temples in the complex, and statues over 1,500 years old have been found here.
Limbus call it Mouksik:Sawalung, the winter residence of the god Dungdung Sammang.

visit.fee_note: No published entry fee found in the sources consulted.

festivals.note_np: विशेष मेला; यस पूर्णिमामा विशेष गरी भारतबाट तीर्थयात्री आउँछन्।

quiz.explanation: Varaha, the boar incarnation, is the main deity.
quiz.q_np: बराहक्षेत्रमा विष्णुको कुन अवतारको पूजा गरिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: वराह, सुँगुर अवतार, मुख्य देवता हुन्।

quiz.q: Which two rivers meet at Barahachhetra?
quiz.explanation: The site lies at the confluence of the Koka and Koshi rivers.
quiz.q_np: बराहक्षेत्रमा कुन दुई नदी मिल्छन्?
quiz.explanation_np: यो स्थान कोका र कोशी नदीको सङ्गममा अवस्थित छ।

quiz.q: Barahachhetra is counted among which group of Nepali pilgrimage sites?
quiz.explanation: It is one of the Char Dham of Nepal.
quiz.q_np: बराहक्षेत्र नेपालका कुन तीर्थस्थल समूहमा गनिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: यो नेपालका चार धाममध्ये एक हो।

quiz.q: Who rebuilt the temple after the 1934 earthquake?
quiz.explanation: Juddha Shumsher rebuilt the temple in 1991 BS.
quiz.q_np: 1934 को भूकम्पपछि मन्दिर कसले पुनर्निर्माण गरे?
quiz.explanation_np: जुद्ध शमशेरले 1991 वि.सं. मा मन्दिर पुनर्निर्माण गरे।

quiz.q: What do Limbu people call Barahachhetra?
quiz.explanation: In Yakthung Limbu belief it is Mouksik:Sawalung, the winter home of Dungdung Sammang.
quiz.q_np: लिम्बू जनजातिले बराहक्षेत्रलाई के भन्छन्?
quiz.explanation_np: याक्थुङ लिम्बू विश्वासमा यो माउक्सिक:सावालुङ हो, दुङदुङ साम्माङको जाडोको बासस्थान।

White domes stand where the Koka pours into the great Koshi, at one of the four great dhams.

short_np: नेपालका चार धाममध्ये एक: कोका र कोशीको संगमस्थलमा विष्णुको वराह अवतारका सेता गुम्बज भएका मन्दिरहरू।
story_np: सुन्नुहोस्: तपाईंको तल, कोका खोला मिसिने ठाउँमा, शक्तिशाली सप्तकोशी पहाडबाट गर्जिँदै निस्किन्छ। तपाईं बराहक्षेत्रमा हुनुहुन्छ, नेपालका चार महान् तीर्थधाममध्ये एक, पुराणमा र महाभारतमा समेत प्रशंसित। कथा भन्छ, एक दानवले पृथ्वीलाई पाताल तर्फ तान्दा, भगवान् विष्णुले वराह, शक्तिशाली बँगुर, को रूप लिए र उनलाई आफ्नो दाह्रामा उठाएर माथि ल्याए। त्यसपछि उनी आफ्नी पत्नी लक्ष्मीसँग यहाँ कोशीको छेउमा विश्राम गरे। पृथ्वी बोकेका वराहको ठूलो मूर्ति खोज्नुहोस्। तपाईंले देख्ने सेतो गुम्बज भएको मन्दिर अपेक्षाकृत नयाँ हो; सन् १९३४ को भूकम्पले पुरानो मन्दिर ढाल्यो, र जुद्ध शमशेरले यसलाई पुनर्निर्माण गराए। तैपनि तपाईंको वरिपरि पन्ध्र सय वर्षभन्दा पुराना मूर्तिहरू भेटिएका छन्। लिम्बू समुदायले यस ठाउँलाई मौक्सिक सावालुङ्ग भन्छन्, देवता डुङ्डुङ सम्माङको जाडोको बासस्थान। कार्तिक पूर्णिमा र माघे संक्रान्तिमा नदीमा नुहाउन भीड आउँछ।
legend_np: पृथ्वीलाई पातालमा तानिँदै गर्दा, विष्णुले बँगुर वराहको रूप लिई उनलाई दाह्रामा उठाएर बाहिर ल्याए, त्यसपछि लक्ष्मीसँग कोशीको किनारमा बसे; ठाउँको नाम त्यही अवतारबाट राखिएको हो।
facts_np: बराहक्षेत्र नेपालका चार धाम (चार महान् तीर्थस्थल) मध्ये एक हो।
यो सुनसरी जिल्लामा कोका र कोशी नदीको संगमस्थलमा पर्छ।
हालको मन्दिर जुद्ध शमशेरले १९९० साल (सन् १९३४) को भूकम्पपछि १९९१ साल मा पुनर्निर्माण गरेका थिए।
परिसरमा नौवटा मन्दिर छन्, र यहाँ १,५०० वर्षभन्दा पुराना मूर्तिहरू भेटिएका छन्।
लिम्बूहरू यसलाई मौक्सिक:सावालुङ्ग भन्छन्, देवता डुङ्डुङ सम्माङको जाडोको निवास।
clues_np: सुँगुरको रूपमा एक देवताले डुब्दै गरेको पृथ्वीलाई दाह्राले उठाए, अनि यहाँ नदीको किनारमा पत्नीसँग विश्राम गरे।
कोका ठूलो कोशीमा मिसिने ठाउँमा सेता गुम्बज उभिएका छन्, चार महान् धाममध्ये एकमा।

name: Tengboche Monastery
coord_source: Wikidata Q7699760 (P625); OpenStreetMap relation 13050800 centroid is 27.836149, 86.763775
built_century_text: Founded in 1916 by Lama Gulu; destroyed by the 1934 earthquake and rebuilt, burnt in a fire on 19 January 1989, rebuilt with international help and reconsecrated in 1993.
architecture: Stone-masonry Tibetan Buddhist gompa with a large courtyard; the Dokhang prayer hall holds a two-storey statue of Shakyamuni flanked by Manjushri and Maitreya. A rebuilt painted entrance gate, mani stones and chortens surround it. Largest gompa in the Khumbu.
short: The largest gompa in the Khumbu, at 3,867 m on the Everest trail, with Everest and Ama Dablam behind it.
story: Take a slow breath; you are at 3,867 metres, on a knoll above the meeting of the Dudh Koshi and Imja rivers. In front of you is Tengboche Monastery, the largest gompa in the Khumbu and home to Sherpa monks of the Nyingma tradition. Lama Gulu founded it in 1916, with blessings from the Rongbuk monastery on the Tibetan side of Everest. Its life has been dramatic. The 1934 earthquake flattened it, and in January 1989 an electrical fire destroyed its old scriptures, statues and murals. Monks, Sherpas and friends from around the world rebuilt it, and it was consecrated again in 1993. Walk through the painted gate and into the prayer hall, where a Buddha rises through two floors. Expeditions stop here to light candles and ask for a safe climb. Now step outside and look up the valley: Everest, Lhotse and the sharp peak of Ama Dablam stand right behind the roof.
legend: Lama Sangwa Dorje, founder of the Pangboche monastery, is said to have foreseen a monastery at Tengboche and left his footprint on a rock while meditating here; the stone fractured in the 1989 fire.
facts: Tengboche stands at 3,867 m and is the largest gompa in the Khumbu region.
It was founded in 1916 by Lama Gulu, linked to the Rongbuk Monastery in Tibet.
It was destroyed by the 1934 earthquake and again by fire on 19 January 1989.
The rebuilt monastery was consecrated in 1993.
The Mani Rimdu festival is held here each autumn.

visit.hours_note: Reached on foot on the Everest Base Camp trail from Lukla via Namche (about 3-4 days). No official hours found in sources.
visit.fee_note: Fees are Sagarmatha National Park entry (foreigners NPR 3,000, SAARC NPR 1,500; Nepali fee reported as free or NPR 100) plus a NPR 2,000 Khumbu Pasang Lhamu rural municipality fee for foreigners.

short_np: खुम्बुको सबैभन्दा ठूलो गुम्बा, एभरेस्ट मार्गमा ३,८६७ मिटरमा, पछाडि एभरेस्ट र अमा दब्लम सहित।
story_np: बिस्तारै सास लिनुहोस्; तपाईं ३,८६७ मिटरमा, दूधकोशी र इम्जा नदीको सङ्गममाथिको टिलामा हुनुहुन्छ। तपाईंको अगाडि टेङबोचे गुम्बा छ, खुम्बुको सबैभन्दा ठूलो गुम्बा र निङ्मा परम्पराका शेर्पा भिक्षुहरूको घर। लामा गुलुले यसलाई सन् १९१६ मा स्थापना गरे, एभरेस्टको तिब्बती पट्टिको रोङ्बुक गुम्बाको आशीर्वादसहित। यसको जीवन नाटकीय रहेको छ। सन् १९३४ को भूकम्पले यसलाई पूरै ढाल्यो, र सन् १९८९ जनवरीमा बिजुलीको आगलागीले यसका पुराना धर्मग्रन्थ, मूर्ति र भित्तेचित्रहरू नष्ट गर्‍यो। भिक्षु, शेर्पा र संसारभरिका मित्रहरूले यसलाई पुनर्निर्माण गरे, र यो सन् १९९३ मा फेरि प्रतिष्ठित गरियो। रङ्गीन ढोकाबाट प्रार्थना कक्षमा हिँड्नुहोस्, जहाँ दुई तलामा उठेको बुद्ध छन्। अभियानहरू यहाँ बत्ती बालेर सुरक्षित आरोहणको कामना गर्न रोकिन्छन्। अब बाहिर निस्केर उपत्यकामाथि हेर्नुहोस्: एभरेस्ट, ल्होत्से र अमा दब्लमको तीखो चुचुरो छानाको ठीक पछाडि उभिएका छन्।
legend_np: पाङ्बोचे गुम्बाका संस्थापक लामा सङ्वा दोर्जेले टेङबोचेमा गुम्बाको पूर्वदर्शन गरेका र यहाँ ध्यान गर्दा चट्टानमा आफ्नो पाइलाको छाप छाडेका थिए भनिन्छ; सन् १९८९ को आगलागीमा त्यो ढुङ्गा चर्कियो।
facts_np: टेङबोचे ३,८६७ मिटरमा छ र खुम्बु क्षेत्रको सबैभन्दा ठूलो गुम्बा हो।
यो सन् १९१६ मा लामा गुलुले स्थापना गरे, तिब्बतको रोङ्बुक गुम्बासँग सम्बन्धित।
यो सन् १९३४ को भूकम्पले र फेरि १९ जनवरी १९८९ मा आगलागीले नष्ट गर्‍यो।
पुनर्निर्मित गुम्बा सन् १९९३ मा प्रतिष्ठित गरियो।
मानी रिम्दु पर्व यहाँ हरेक शरदमा मनाइन्छ।
clues_np: पृथ्वीको सबैभन्दा अग्लो शिखरतिर लाग्नुअघि आरोहीहरू यहाँ बत्ती बाल्छन्; त्यो शिखर मेरो छानामाथि झुलुक्क देखिन्छ।
1934 मा हल्लिएर ढलेँ, 1989 मा जलेँ, संसारभरिको सहयोगले फेरि उठेँ र 1993 मा पुनः प्रतिष्ठा गरियो।

name: Dantakali Temple
built_century_text: Founder unknown; scriptures say a king of Bengal repaired it. A pagoda until the 1934 earthquake, rebuilt with a dome, damaged again in the 1988 earthquake and restored to pagoda form.
architecture: Small two-roofed pagoda with grey roofs, red-orange walls and a gilded pinnacle inside a whitewashed walled compound entered through an arched red gateway on Bijayapur hill. The pagoda form was restored after the 1988 earthquake toppled an earlier dome (gumbaj) roof.
short: Shakti Peeth on Bijayapur hill in Dharan, said to mark where the tooth of the goddess Sati fell.
story: Climb the steps of Bijayapur hill above Dharan and pass under the arched red gate. You have come to Dantakali, one of the Shakti Peethas, the places where pieces of the goddess Sati fell to earth. When Sati gave up her life, grieving Shiva wandered the world carrying her body, and parts of it dropped across the land. Here, devotees believe, fell her tooth: danta means tooth, so this is the temple of the tooth of Kali. The Swasthani Bratakatha, a scripture many Nepali families read each winter, mentions this place. The building has had a hard century. It was a pagoda until the earthquake of 1934 knocked it down. It came back with a dome roof, which the 1988 earthquake toppled in turn, and then it was rebuilt as the pagoda you see. Budhasubba and Pindeshwor are both a short walk away. At Dashain the queue of worshippers stretches down the hill.
legend: As Shiva carried the dead body of Sati across the world, her tooth (danta) fell at this spot, making it a Shakti Peeth.
facts: The temple's name comes from danta (tooth) and Kali; it marks where Sati's tooth is believed to have fallen.
It is mentioned in the Swasthani Bratakatha.
It was a pagoda until the 1934 earthquake, then had a dome roof that fell in the 1988 earthquake.
It lies about 1 km from Pindeshwor and 1.5 km from Budhasubba on Bijayapur hill.

quiz.q: What does 'danta' in Dantakali mean?
quiz.explanation: Danta means tooth; Sati's tooth is believed to have fallen here.
quiz.q_np: दन्तकालीमा ‘दन्त’ को अर्थ के हो?
quiz.explanation_np: दन्त भनेको दाँत; यहाँ सतीको दाँत खसेको विश्वास गरिन्छ।

quiz.q: In which city is Dantakali Temple?

quiz.q_np: दन्तकाली मन्दिर कुन सहरमा छ?

quiz.q: Dantakali is counted as one of the what?
quiz.explanation: It is a Shakti Peeth, a place where part of Sati's body fell.
quiz.q_np: दन्तकालीलाई कुनमध्ये एक मानिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: यो शक्तिपीठ हो, अर्थात् सतीको शरीरको अङ्ग खसेको ठाउँ।

quiz.q: Which scripture mentions this temple?
quiz.explanation: The Swasthani Bratakatha mentions Dantakali.
quiz.q_np: कुन धर्मग्रन्थमा यस मन्दिरको उल्लेख छ?
quiz.explanation_np: स्वस्थानी व्रतकथामा दन्तकालीको उल्लेख छ।

quiz.q: Which earthquake brought down the temple's dome-style roof?
quiz.explanation: The 1988 earthquake toppled the gumbaj roof, and the temple was restored as a pagoda.
quiz.q_np: कुन भूकम्पले मन्दिरको गुम्बज शैलीको छाना ढाल्यो?
quiz.explanation_np: सन् 1988 को भूकम्पले गुम्बजको छाना ढाल्यो, र मन्दिर पगोडा शैलीमा पुनर्निर्माण गरियो।

clues: When a grieving god carried his wife's body across the world, her tooth is said to have dropped on this hill.
Pagoda, then dome, then pagoda again: two earthquakes, in 1934 and 1988, keep changing my roof.

story_np: धरानमाथिको बिजयपुर डाँडाका सिँढी चढ्नुहोस् र मेहराब आकारको रातो ढोकामुनि पार गर्नुहोस्। तपाईं दन्तकालीमा आइपुग्नुभएको छ, शक्तिपीठहरूमध्ये एक, जहाँ सती देवीका अङ्गहरू पृथ्वीमा खसेका थिए। सतीले प्राण त्यागेपछि शोकाकुल शिव उनको शव बोकेर संसारभर घुमे, र अङ्गहरू देशभर खसे। यहाँ, भक्तजनको विश्वास अनुसार, उनको दाँत खस्यो: दन्तको अर्थ दाँत हो, त्यसैले यो कालीको दाँतको मन्दिर हो। धेरै नेपाली परिवारले हरेक जाडोमा पढ्ने स्वस्थानी व्रतकथामा यो ठाउँको उल्लेख छ। भवनले एक कठिन शताब्दी बिताएको छ। 1934 को भूकम्पले ढाल्नुअघि यो पगोडा थियो। यो गुम्बजको छानासहित फर्कियो, जसलाई 1988 को भूकम्पले पालैपालो ढालिदियो, र त्यसपछि तपाईंले देख्नुभएको पगोडा रूपमा पुनर्निर्माण गरियो। बुढासुब्बा र पिण्डेश्वर दुवै छोटो पैदल दूरीमा छन्। दशैँमा भक्तजनको लाइन डाँडाभर तलसम्म फैलिन्छ।
legend_np: शिवले सतीको मृत शरीर बोकेर संसारभर घुम्दा उनको दाँत (दन्त) यही ठाउँमा खस्यो, र यो शक्तिपीठ बन्यो।
facts_np: मन्दिरको नाम दन्त (दाँत) र कालीबाट आएको हो; सतीको दाँत खसेको मानिने ठाउँलाई यसले जनाउँछ।
यो स्वस्थानी व्रतकथामा उल्लेख गरिएको छ।
1934 को भूकम्पसम्म यो पगोडा थियो, त्यसपछि गुम्बजको छाना भयो जुन 1988 को भूकम्पमा ढल्यो।
यो बिजयपुर डाँडामा पिण्डेश्वरबाट करिब 1 किलोमिटर र बुढासुब्बाबाट 1.5 किलोमिटर दूरीमा छ।
clues_np: शोकाकुल देवताले पत्नीको शरीर बोकेर संसार घुम्दा यही डाँडामा उनको दाँत खसेको भनिन्छ।
पगोडा, त्यसपछि गुम्बज, फेरि पगोडा: सन् 1934 र 1988 का दुई भूकम्पले मेरो छाना बदलिरहे।

name: Budha Subba Temple

deity: Budha Subba (spirit of the Limbu king Buddhi Karna Raya Khebang); also linked with Shiva and Parvati as Theba Sammang and Yuma Sammang
built_century_text: Said to be the tomb of Buddhi Karna Raya Khebang, last Limbu king of Bijaypur, killed in 1773; date of the shrine itself not documented.
architecture: Small Kirat shrine on Bijayapur hill: an open pavilion with a low hipped roof and red pillars beside a yellow arched shrine, set in a grove of tuftless bamboo hung with sacred threads and bells.
short: Kirat shrine in a bamboo grove in Dharan, said to be the tomb of the last Limbu king of Bijaypur.
story: Step into the bamboo grove on Bijayapur hill in Dharan and listen to the stems creak in the wind. This is Budha Subba, a shrine of the Kirat people, and its story is a sad one. Bijaypur was once a capital of the Limbuwan kingdom. In 1773 its last Limbu king, Buddhi Karna Raya Khebang, was lured here for talks and killed by assassins sent by the Gorkhali king. People say his spirit stayed near his tomb, friendly and helpful, and local Limbus began to worship him as the old king, the Budha Subba, who brings good luck. Now look closely at the bamboo. Some say Shiva and Parvati, disguised as a Limbu king and queen, once planted their hunting bows here, and these bamboos grew from them without tufts at the top. Young couples used to carve their names on the stems; today they tie colourful threads instead and hope their love lasts.
legend: Shiva and Parvati, in the guise of the Yakthung king and queen Theba Sammang and Yuma Sammang, stuck their bows into the ground here while hunting; tuftless bamboo sprouted from the bows.
facts: The shrine is said to be the tomb of Buddhi Karna Raya Khebang, the last Limbu king of Bijaypur, killed in 1773.
Bijaypur was a capital of the Limbuwan kingdom according to historian Iman Singh Chemjong.
The bamboo here grows without a tuft at the top, which legend links to Shiva and Parvati's bows.
Couples once wrote their names on the bamboo; the temple committee stopped this, and threads are tied instead.

A Limbu king lured to peace talks never left this hill; his kindly spirit is worshipped here instead.

short_np: धरानको बाँसघारीभित्रको किराँत मन्दिर, विजयपुरका अन्तिम लिम्बू राजाको समाधि भनिने।
story_np: धरानको विजयपुर डाँडाको बाँसघारीभित्र पस्नुहोस् र हावामा बाँसका ठाँटहरू चर्कँदै गरेको सुन्नुहोस्। यो बुढासुब्बा हो, किराँत जातिको मन्दिर, र यसको कथा दुःखद छ। विजयपुर कुनै समय लिम्बूवान राज्यको राजधानी थियो। सन् 1773 मा यसका अन्तिम लिम्बू राजा बुद्धिकर्ण राय खेबाङलाई वार्ताका लागि यहाँ बोलाइयो र गोर्खाली राजाले पठाएका हत्याराहरूले मारे। मानिसहरू भन्छन् उनको आत्मा उनको समाधिनजिकै बस्यो, मित्रवत् र सहयोगी, र स्थानीय लिम्बूहरूले उनलाई बुढा सुब्बा, शुभ भाग्य ल्याउने पुराना राजाका रूपमा पूजा गर्न थाले। अब बाँसलाई नजिकबाट हेर्नुहोस्। कसैले भन्छन्, लिम्बू राजा र रानीको भेषमा शिव र पार्वतीले यहीँ आफ्ना सिकारका धनुष रोपेका थिए, र यी बाँस तिनैबाट टुप्पोमा झुप्पा बिना उम्रे। जवान जोडीहरू बाँसका ठाँटमा आफ्ना नाम कुँद्थे; आज तिनीहरू रङ्गीन धागो बाँध्छन् र आफ्नो माया टिकिरहोस् भन्ने आशा गर्छन्।
legend_np: याक्थुङ राजा र रानी थेबा साम्माङ र युमा साम्माङको रूपमा शिव र पार्वतीले सिकार खेल्दा यहाँ भुइँमा आफ्ना धनुष रोपे; ती धनुषबाट झुप्पा नभएको बाँस उम्रियो।
facts_np: यो मन्दिर विजयपुरका अन्तिम लिम्बू राजा बुद्धिकर्ण राय खेबाङको समाधि भनिन्छ, जसलाई सन् 1773 मा मारिएको थियो।
इतिहासकार इमानसिंह चेमजोङका अनुसार विजयपुर लिम्बूवान राज्यको एक राजधानी थियो।
यहाँको बाँस टुप्पोमा झुप्पा बिना उम्रन्छ, जसलाई किंवदन्तीले शिव र पार्वतीका धनुषसँग जोड्छ।
जोडीहरूले एक समय बाँसमा आफ्ना नाम लेख्थे; मन्दिर समितिले यो रोक्यो, र अब धागो बाँधिन्छ।
clues_np: प्रेमीहरूले कुनै बेला मेरो बाँसमा नाम कुँदे; अहिले झुप्पा नहुने बाँसका डाँठमा उनीहरू रङ्गीन धागो बाँध्छन्।
शान्तिवार्तामा बोलाइएका एक लिम्बू राजा यो डाँडाबाट कहिल्यै फर्किएनन्; यहाँ उनको दयालु आत्माको पूजा गरिन्छ।

name: Pindeshwor Babadham
built_century_text: Founding date not documented in the sources consulted; local scholar Prem Prasad Parajuli says the temple is mentioned in 18 chapters of the Skanda Purana.
architecture: Orange-painted shikhara-style Shiva temple with a tall spire and trident, joined to a long arcaded hall of arched openings, in a walled compound in Dharan-14. Oil lamps are kept burning continuously inside.
short: Shiva temple in Dharan where Shrawan pilgrims walk barefoot from Barahachhetra carrying Koshi water to pour on the lingam.
story: You are at Pindeshwor Babadham in Dharan, a temple of Lord Shiva that comes alive in the monsoon month of Shrawan. Every Monday of that month, thousands of devotees arrive on foot, many barefoot, chanting Bol Bam. They have walked more than twenty kilometres from Barahachhetra, carrying pots of holy water from the Saptakoshi river, to pour over Shiva here. Devotees say wishes come true if you offer Koshi and Koka water at Barahachhetra, then water from the Kaushiki bank here at Pindeshwor. Look up at the orange spire and its trident, then at the long row of arches beside it. Inside, oil lamps are never allowed to go out. A local scholar says this place appears in eighteen chapters of the Skanda Purana, and people also link it to the origin of rudraksha beads. Dantakali and Budhasubba are just up the hill, so many pilgrims visit all three together.
legend: Local belief links the site to the origin of rudraksha beads and says it appears in 18 chapters of the Skanda Purana.
facts: On every Monday of Shrawan, devotees carry Saptakoshi water from Barahachhetra, many walking barefoot over 20 km.
Oil lamps are kept burning continuously in the temple.
Maha Shivaratri and Bala Chaturdashi are also major festivals here.
A Pindeshwor Rath Yatra chariot festival around Dharan Bazaar was held for the second time in March 2026.

short_np: धरानको शिव मन्दिर जहाँ श्रावणमा तीर्थयात्रीहरू बराहक्षेत्रबाट खालि खुट्टा कोशीको पानी बोकेर शिवलिङ्गमा चढाउन हिँड्छन्।
story_np: तपाईं धरानको पिण्डेश्वर बाबाधाममा हुनुहुन्छ, भगवान् शिवको मन्दिर जो वर्षा महिना श्रावणमा जीवन्त हुन्छ। त्यस महिनाको हरेक सोमबार, हजारौँ भक्तजन 'बोल बम' जप्दै हिँडेर आइपुग्छन्, धेरैजना खालि खुट्टा। उनीहरू बराहक्षेत्रबाट बीस किलोमिटरभन्दा बढी हिँडेका हुन्छन्, सप्तकोशी नदीको पवित्र जलको घडा बोकेर, यहाँ शिवलाई चढाउन। भक्तजनहरू भन्छन् बराहक्षेत्रमा कोशी र कोकाको पानी चढाएर, त्यसपछि यहाँ पिण्डेश्वरमा कौशिकी किनारको पानी चढाए मनोकामना पूरा हुन्छ। सुन्तला रङको शिखर र त्रिशूलमा माथि हेर्नुहोस्, अनि छेउको मेहराबहरूको लामो पङ्क्तिमा। भित्र, तेलका दीपहरू कहिल्यै निभ्न दिइँदैन। एक स्थानीय विद्वान भन्छन् यो ठाउँ स्कन्द पुराणका अठारह अध्यायमा देखा पर्छ, र मानिसहरू यसलाई रुद्राक्ष मालाको उत्पत्तिसँग पनि जोड्छन्। दन्तकाली र बुढासुब्बा डाँडामाथि नै छन्, त्यसैले धेरै तीर्थयात्रीहरू तीनवटै सँगै दर्शन गर्छन्।
legend_np: स्थानीय विश्वासले यो स्थललाई रुद्राक्ष मालाको उत्पत्तिसँग जोड्छ र यो स्कन्द पुराणका १८ अध्यायमा देखा पर्छ भन्छ।
facts_np: श्रावणको हरेक सोमबार, भक्तजनहरू बराहक्षेत्रबाट सप्तकोशीको पानी बोकेर २० कि.मी. भन्दा बढी हिँड्छन्, धेरैजना खालि खुट्टा।
मन्दिरमा तेलका दीपहरू निरन्तर बलिरहन्छन्।
महाशिवरात्रि र बाला चतुर्दशी पनि यहाँका प्रमुख चाड हुन्।
धरान बजारको वरिपरि पिण्डेश्वर रथयात्रा, रथको चाड, दोस्रो पटक मार्च २०२६ मा मनाइएको थियो।
clues_np: वर्षा महिनाको हरेक सोमबार खाली खुट्टा भक्तजनहरू नदीबाट मेरो लिङ्गका लागि जल बोकेर बीस किलोमिटर हिँड्छन्।
मेरो सुन्तला रङको शिखरपछाडि मेहराबको लामो पङ्क्ति छ, र भित्र तेलका दियाहरू कहिल्यै निभ्न दिइँदैन।

name: Makwanpur Gadhi
built_century_text: Stronghold of the Sen kings of Makwanpur; Wikipedia credits Tula Sen, while Ekantipur says Luhang built it in VS 1622 (c. 1565). Captured by Gorkha in VS 1819 (1762-63).
architecture: Hilltop stone fort at about 1,017 m, surrounded by a wall about 25 ft high and 7 ft wide and a 10-ft-deep defensive ditch, enclosing the ruined walls of the Sen palace. Old cannons such as the 'Kali Top' are displayed in the grounds.
short: Hilltop stone fort of the Sen kings near Hetauda, fought over by Gorkha in 1762-63 and by the British in 1816.
story: You are standing inside Makwanpur Gadhi, about 1,000 metres up on a ridge east of Hetauda. Before Nepal was unified, this stone fort was the stronghold of the Sen kings of Makwanpur. Run your hand along the wall: it once rose about 25 feet and was 7 feet thick, with a ditch 10 feet deep outside to stop attackers. The Sens and the Shahs were family. King Hemkarna Sen's daughter, Indra Kumari, married Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha. Yet family ties did not keep the peace. Prithvi Narayan Shah's forces attacked and took this fort in 1762, and fought here again the next year against the army of Mir Kasim, the Nawab of Bengal. In 1816 it saw battle once more, in the war with the British East India Company. Look for the old iron cannon called Kali Top. In 2015 Nepal Post put this fort on a postage stamp.
legend: Ekantipur reports a story that Hemkarna Sen promised a white elephant as dowry to his son-in-law Prithvi Narayan Shah, but his son Digbandhan Sen refused to hand it over, souring relations before the conquest.
facts: The fort was the main stronghold of the Sen dynasty of Makwanpur before Nepal's unification.
Battles of Makwanpur were fought here in 1762, 1763 and 1816.
Its wall is described as about 25 ft high and 7 ft wide, with a 10-ft-deep defensive ditch.
It sits at about 1,017 m, roughly 16-17 km from Hetauda.
The Government of Nepal issued a postage stamp featuring the fort in 2015.

quiz.explanation: The fort was the stronghold of the Sen kings of Makwanpur.

quiz.explanation_np: गढी मकवानपुरका सेन राजाहरूको किल्ला थियो।

quiz.q: Which Gorkha king married a Makwanpur princess and later captured the fort?
quiz.explanation: Prithvi Narayan Shah married Indra Kumari and took Makwanpur in 1762-63.
quiz.q_np: कुन गोरखा राजाले मकवानपुरकी राजकुमारीसँग विवाह गरी पछि गढी कब्जा गरे?
quiz.explanation_np: पृथ्वीनारायण शाहले इन्द्रकुमारीसँग विवाह गरे र 1762-63 मा मकवानपुर लिए।

quiz.q: Against whom was the 1816 Battle of Makwanpur fought?
quiz.explanation: The 1816 battle was part of the Anglo-Nepalese War.
quiz.q_np: 1816 को मकवानपुरको युद्ध कसको विरुद्ध लडिएको थियो?
quiz.explanation_np: 1816 को युद्ध अङ्ग्रेज-नेपाल युद्धको भाग थियो।

quiz.q: What is the name of the famous old cannon at the fort?
quiz.explanation: The historic cannon displayed at the fort is called Kali Top.
quiz.q_np: गढीको प्रसिद्ध पुरानो तोपको नाम के हो?
quiz.explanation_np: गढीमा प्रदर्शनमा राखिएको ऐतिहासिक तोपलाई कालीतोप भनिन्छ।

quiz.q: In which year did Nepal issue a stamp featuring Makwanpur Gadhi?
quiz.explanation: The Government of Nepal issued the stamp in 2015.
quiz.q_np: नेपालले मकवानपुरगढी भएको हुलाक टिकट कुन वर्ष जारी गर्‍यो?
quiz.explanation_np: नेपाल सरकारले 2015 मा टिकट जारी गरेको थियो।

clues: A Gorkha king married a princess of this hilltop fort, then came back with an army to capture it.
Three battles in 1762, 1763 and 1816 echoed off my 25-foot stone walls above Hetauda.

short_np: हेटौँडा नजिकको सेन राजाहरूको डाँडाको ढुङ्गाको किल्ला, जसका लागि सन् १७६२-६३ मा गोर्खा र सन् १८१६ मा अङ्ग्रेजहरूले लडे।
story_np: तपाईं हेटौँडाको पूर्वको डाँडामा करिब १,००० मिटर माथि मकवानपुरगढीभित्र उभिनुभएको छ। नेपाल एकीकरण हुनुअघि यो ढुङ्गाको किल्ला मकवानपुरका सेन राजाहरूको गढ थियो। भित्तामा हात फेर्नुहोस्: यो कुनै बेला करिब २५ फिट अग्लो र ७ फिट बाक्लो थियो, आक्रमणकारी रोक्न बाहिर १० फिट गहिरो खाल्डो थियो। सेन र शाह नातेदार थिए। राजा हेमकर्ण सेनकी छोरी इन्द्र कुमारीले गोरखाका पृथ्वीनारायण शाहसँग विवाह गरिन्। तैपनि पारिवारिक सम्बन्धले शान्ति कायम राखेन। पृथ्वीनारायण शाहका सेनाहरूले सन् १७६२ मा यो किल्ला आक्रमण गरी कब्जा गरे, र अर्को वर्ष बङ्गालका नवाब मीर कासिमको सेनाविरुद्ध यहीँ फेरि लडे। सन् १८१६ मा, ब्रिटिश ईस्ट इन्डिया कम्पनीसँगको युद्धमा यसले फेरि लडाइँ देख्यो। काली तोप भनिने पुरानो फलामको तोप खोज्नुहोस्। सन् २०१५ मा नेपाल हुलाकले यो किल्लालाई हुलाक टिकटमा राख्यो।
legend_np: एकान्तिपुरले एउटा कथा रिपोर्ट गर्छ कि हेमकर्ण सेनले ज्वाइँ पृथ्वीनारायण शाहलाई दाइजोमा सेतो हात्ती दिने वचन दिएका थिए, तर उनका छोरा दिग्बन्धन सेनले दिन इन्कार गरे, जसले विजयअघि सम्बन्ध बिगारेको थियो।
facts_np: किल्ला नेपाल एकीकरणअघि मकवानपुरको सेन वंशको मुख्य गढ थियो।
मकवानपुरका युद्धहरू यहाँ सन् १७६२, १७६३ र १८१६ मा लडिए।
यसको पर्खाल करिब २५ फिट अग्लो र ७ फिट चौडा, १० फिट गहिरो सुरक्षात्मक खाल्डोसहित भनिएको छ।
यो करिब १,०१७ मिटरमा छ, हेटौँडाबाट करिब १६-१७ किमी।
नेपाल सरकारले सन् २०१५ मा यो किल्ला भएको हुलाक टिकट जारी गर्‍यो।
clues_np: एक गोरखा राजाले यो डाँडाको किल्लाकी राजकुमारीसँग विवाह गरे, अनि सेना लिएर फर्केर त्यसलाई कब्जा गरे।
1762, 1763 र 1816 का तीन युद्धको प्रतिध्वनि हेटौँडामाथिको मेरा 25 फिट अग्ला ढुङ्गाका पर्खालमा गुञ्जिए।

name: Upardang Gadhi
built_century_text: Sources differ: Nepal Traveller credits Shatrubhanjan Shah, grandson of Prithvi Narayan Shah, during the war with the British; Ekantipur links it to the Sen era. It was Chitwan's headquarters until the early 1960s.
architecture: Hilltop fort at about 1,275 m enclosed by a carved stone wall, with a weapon house (Kot Ghar), a well, a two-room house, a gate, a wooden bridge and a temple inside; the Department of Archaeology notes its walls, defensive ditch and entry tunnel.
short: Stone hill fort above the Chitwan valley, once the valley's capital and Chitwan's district headquarters until the 1960s.
story: You have climbed to Upardang Gadhi, 1,275 metres up in the hills of northern Chitwan, about an hour's ride from Bharatpur. Look down: the whole Chitwan valley spreads out below, and this is why the fort was built here. Before Nepal's unification, this valley was its own small kingdom, and its historic capital was right here at Upardang. Walk along the low stone walls. Historians do not fully agree on who built them. One account credits Shatrubhanjan Shah, grandson of Prithvi Narayan Shah, who strengthened the fort during the war with the British; another links it to the earlier Sen kings. Inside, find the old weapon house, the well and the small temple. Until the early 1960s this was Chitwan's district headquarters, and land revenue was collected here long after. Cannons and shells have been recovered from the site, and restoration began in 2023 with the Department of Archaeology.
facts: Before Nepal's unification, Upardanggadhi was the historic capital of the Chitwan valley kingdom.
The fort sits at about 1,275 m above sea level.
It was Chitwan's district headquarters until the early 1960s, before the move to Bharatpur.
Cannons, shells and old weapons have been recovered from the fort.
Renovation in coordination with the Department of Archaeology began in 2023.

visit.hours_note: Open-air hill fort in ward 7 of Ichchhakamana Rural Municipality, about an hour by road from Bharatpur; no official hours found.

quiz.q: Upardang Gadhi was the historic capital of which valley?

quiz.q_np: उपरदाङगढी कुन उपत्यकाको ऐतिहासिक राजधानी थियो?

quiz.explanation: The headquarters moved to Bharatpur after the early 1960s.
quiz.q_np: किल्ला करिब कहिलेसम्म चितवनको जिल्ला सदरमुकाम थियो?
quiz.explanation_np: 1960 को दशकको सुरुपछि सदरमुकाम भरतपुर सरेको थियो।

quiz.explanation_np: किल्ला समुद्र सतहबाट करिब 1,275 m माथि छ।

quiz.q: Which grandson of Prithvi Narayan Shah is credited by one source with building the fort?
quiz.explanation: Nepal Traveller credits Shatrubhanjan Shah, son of Bahadur Shah.
quiz.q_np: एउटा स्रोतले पृथ्वीनारायण शाहका कुन नातिलाई किल्ला निर्माणको श्रेय दिन्छ?
quiz.explanation_np: नेपाल ट्राभलरले बहादुर शाहका छोरा शत्रुभञ्जन शाहलाई श्रेय दिएको छ।

clues: From my stone walls high in the hills you can see the whole jungle valley I once ruled as its capital.
District officials worked inside my walls until the 1960s, when they moved down to the plains at Bharatpur.

short_np: चितवन उपत्यकामाथिको ढुङ्गाको डाँडे किल्ला, एक समय उपत्यकाको राजधानी र 1960 को दशकसम्म चितवनको जिल्ला सदरमुकाम।
story_np: तपाईं चितवनको उत्तरी डाँडामा 1,275 मिटर उचाइको उपरदाङगढीमा चढ्नुभएको छ, भरतपुरबाट करिब एक घण्टाको सवारीमा। तल हेर्नुहोस्: सारा चितवन उपत्यका तल फैलिएको छ, र यही कारणले यहाँ किल्ला बनाइएको थियो। नेपाल एकीकरणअघि यो उपत्यका आफ्नै सानो राज्य थियो, र यसको ऐतिहासिक राजधानी यहीँ उपरदाङमा थियो। होचा ढुङ्गाका पर्खालसँगै हिँड्नुहोस्। इतिहासकारहरू कसले बनाए भन्नेमा पूर्ण सहमत छैनन्। एउटा वृत्तान्तले पृथ्वीनारायण शाहका नाति शत्रुभञ्जन शाहलाई श्रेय दिन्छ, जसले बेलायतसँगको युद्धमा किल्ला बलियो बनाए; अर्कोले यसलाई अघिका सेन राजाहरूसँग जोड्छ। भित्र पुरानो हतियार घर, इनार र सानो मन्दिर खोज्नुहोस्। 1960 को दशकको सुरुवातसम्म यो चितवनको जिल्ला सदरमुकाम थियो, र त्यसपछि पनि लामो समय यहीँ मालपोत उठाइन्थ्यो। यस स्थलबाट तोप र गोला बरामद भएका छन्, र पुरातत्त्व विभागसँग मिलेर 2023 मा पुनर्स्थापना सुरु भयो।
facts_np: नेपाल एकीकरणअघि उपरदाङगढी चितवन उपत्यका राज्यको ऐतिहासिक राजधानी थियो।
किल्ला समुद्री सतहबाट करिब 1,275 मिटर उचाइमा छ।
भरतपुर सरेसम्म, 1960 को दशकको सुरुवातसम्म, यो चितवनको जिल्ला सदरमुकाम थियो।
